repo.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.
repo.name: sglang

detail.body:
## Motivation

Elastic EP today grows a serving deployment and recovers a rank that has dropped out.
This PR adds the third direction: **retiring live ranks from a deployment that keeps
serving**. Both directions are expressed on the same `active_ranks` bitmask, so a shrink
and a later grow are the same mask operation viewed from opposite ends, and a deployment
can move freely between widths under an orchestrator's control.

The driving use case is a Kubernetes reconciler reclaiming GPUs from an underloaded
deployment (Dynamo DEP #13121, RFC #35376, raised by @julienmancuso). That needs three
things from a shrink: in flight requests finish, the interruption is small enough not to
read as an outage, and the orchestrator gets a positive "this rank may now be terminated"
signal rather than having to infer it from a process exit. All three are addressed here.

On DeepSeek-V3-Lite FP8, one H100 node, 8 concurrent streams, a 4 → 3 shrink keeps
serving throughout at **8.9 ms p50 inter token latency, a 13 ms peak stall across the
reconfiguration, and a 4.1 s settle to the new width**.

## Modifications

### A scale down state machine on the active_ranks mask

`elastic_ep/scale_down_state.py` adds a per rank FSM driving
`PREPARE → DRAIN → NIXL_RETIRE → FLIP_MASK`, then `RECONFIG → COMPLETE` on a survivor and
`LOCAL_CLEANUP → EXIT` on a retiree. The tick runs at the top of the event loops, ahead of
`recv_requests`, so every rank issues its control broadcasts from the same point in the
iteration.

The side effects each transition needs sit beside the machine rather than in the runner.
`scale_down_driver.py` maps transitions onto those effects and takes the two runner owned
tails as callables, `scale_down_finalizer.py` holds the survivor rebuild sequence and
returns what it wants written, and `expert_map_repair.py` owns the map truncation and orphan
repair. `model_runner.py` constructs them, delegates, and applies the three fields the
finalizer hands back.

Both cohort barriers rendezvous over the global TCPStore and are polled across ticks, so a
rank waiting on one keeps servicing `mlp_sync` for peers that have not arrived yet. Host
agreement is all the barrier owes — the quiesce that protects the retiree is a local CUDA
synchronize before the NIXL disconnect.

Leaving `DRAIN` is a cohort decision carried on the `mlp_sync` the cohort already runs each
iteration: ranks cross only on a unanimous answer, which every rank reads in the same
iteration, and the batch step gate closes at that crossing. The shrink path
expert location broadcast is dropped with it — every survivor derives the same map by
applying the same deterministic repair to an agreed pre shrink map, so it already holds
what the broadcast would have sent.

### Requests in flight finish before their rank leaves

A retiring rank withholds its drain barrier arrival until its own queues are empty.
Survivors keep serving while they wait, and `/scale_elastic_ep` has already closed the
tokenizer admission gate for the departing slots, so their queues only drain while the
slots that are staying keep taking new work; `elastic_ep_scale_timeout` bounds it. Gating
server wide instead would let one long decode pinned to a retiring rank block admissions
everywhere for as long as it runs.
The idleness predicate is cached on the `ModelRunner` when the scheduler first supplies it,
so the forward path entry point observes the same gate as the scheduler path one. The
barrier recheck is a non blocking probe throttled by wall clock, which keeps a rank that is
still decoding at full decode speed while it waits.

One consequence of a resize completing a scatter call short. A survivor that was slow to
reply is still owed, and that reply used to land in the next call's result bucket, both
corrupting it and able to complete it early. The finished call now holds its bucket open
briefly, under the same lock the request is sent from, so no later call's bucket exists yet
and anything arriving is stale by construction. A reply slower than that window still
escapes; closing it needs the reply to name the call it answers, which none of these
payloads carry today.

### Ranks leave the group deliberately

A retiring rank proposes its own removal through `mooncake.pg.deactivate_ranks` as its
final Mooncake call, so the coordinator drops it on request instead of discovering its
absence through link timeouts. This takes a ~10 s per peer fault timeout out of every
shrink and brings reconfiguration from 11–12 s down to under 2 s. Only the retiree
proposes, and only for itself, which keeps it a full participant in the barriers it is
still inside. Because a deliberate departure raises no fault, the device is quiesced before
the NIXL disconnect and survivors wait on `get_peer_state` before any post flip collective.

The retiree then tears down its backends explicitly before exiting, so Mooncake's
destructors run against a live CUDA driver.

### The expert map and its weights follow the slots

`physical_to_logical_map` moves over the TCPStore, one inbox per reader, emptied as it is
read — freshness is the key's absence between rounds, which stays correct across a cohort
that changes width on every call. A joiner clears its inbox before announcing itself, so
only this scale's map can be read from its slot.

Relabelling a physical slot is only half the job, and both directions relabel: a shrink
repairs logical experts whose replicas lived on retiring ranks onto surviving slots
(262–531 experts per shrink at these widths), and a grow stamps real logical ids on
appended slots. Each side reloads its own weights from the backup client or disk once the
new metadata is installed, against the authoritative map it receives rather than the layout
it computed at startup. Slots the p2p could not source are left for that reload and
reported, rather than being published with a temp buffer's contents.

`EPLBManager.reshuffle_for_scale` then runs a load aware rebalance from the scale
finalizer, since a shrink concentrates the same logical experts onto fewer ranks. Its
go/no-go prechecks are decided by a TCPStore cohort vote rather than a device all-reduce,
and any post scale layout is sized from the installed metadata rather than launch time
args. Periodic EPLB is rearmed for the post shrink phase so a shrunk deployment keeps
adapting.

### Decode CUDA graphs survive a shrink

This is where the latency numbers come from — elastic EP previously ran all-eager, measured
at 7.3x decode cost.

A captured decode graph replays against the storage it recorded, so a scale must rewrite
the dispatch tensors in place rather than reallocate them. Three reads reach the expert map
from inside a captured graph and only one has a shape a scale moves:
`partial_logical_to_all_physical_map`, indexed `[topk_ids, chosen_dispatch_index]`, whose
last dim is the replica fan out. Padding that fan out to a width `--max-ep-size` fixes, and
adopting a rescaled map through `adopt_scaled_in_place` (`copy_` into the existing tensors,
the in place discipline `update()` already uses for EPLB rebalance), makes a shrink a no-op
for the graph.

The DP num token buffers a graph gathers over are held at the same pool ceiling
(`dp_capacity_for`), with the fill writing only the slots that have a live rank behind them
and zeroing the rest, so a retired slot reads as a rank contributing no tokens. Retirees are
the contiguous tail, and the MAX_LEN layout used inside graphs strides by a fixed per rank
length, so no surviving rank's offset moves.

In place adoption is what keeps a replay *valid* across the width change, but it does not
by itself make the graph current: the post shrink `reshuffle_for_scale` reinstalls the
expert layout, and `num_physical_experts` is captured as a scalar. So the shrink rebuilds
the decode graphs too, after the reshuffle, so the capture sees the layout that will
actually serve. The finalizer requests the rebuild and `tick_elastic_scale` runs it, at the
top of the event loop: with `max_ep_size == tp_size` the finalizer itself runs at the tail
of `forward()`, where dropping the graph memory pool would invalidate the output that
forward is about to return. This is gated separately from the grow side recapture, which requires
`max_ep_size > tp_size`; a shrink only cohort runs `max_ep_size == tp_size` and is exactly
the configuration that keeps its graphs, so it needs the rebuild most.

With graphs live, the drain barrier probes rather than waiting in place (`keep_serving`),
which is what its module docstring already described: every peer is still serving there,
and a zero width probe folds within the tick when they are already posted. The NIXL fold
keeps its window — past `on_depart_drain` the peers have gated their batch step, so waiting
there costs no tokens and is what makes the same tick crossing `_advance` relies on true.

### A grow reports done only once the joiner can serve

Everything that lets a joiner take part in an a2a — KV-cache allocation, NIXL buffer
creation, the prefill shape DeepGEMM JIT that only compiles once a kernel runs — happens
after its `ModelRunner.__init__`, and measures 37 s quiet, up to 68 s under load. A grow
therefore commits into a `warming_up` phase and reports done only once a forward has
returned at the new width, which proves the joiner took part because dispatch is
collective. An idle cohort has no forward coming, so the window is bounded by a deadline;
grows never close the admission gate, so traffic keeps flowing and settles it promptly.

A grow that crosses the launch width needs both a `recover_ranks` batch and a fresh join,
and `_activate` takes one `include_subgroups` flag per batch. The tokenizer manager now
derives both stages itself against the launch width, holding `pending_ep_size` at the
caller's target so a poller only ever sees the finished width reported as finished. The
second stage goes out on the first's completion, which the schedulers already withhold
until the grow leaves `warming_up`.

A grow that stays below the launch width is different, and goes direct. A recover joiner
covers `[ep_join_rank_offset, ep_join_rank_offset + tp_size)` and sizes its expert map to
that upper bound, so only a target short of that span needs an intermediate; one booted at
exactly the target does not, and that is the common case. Since nothing on the survivor
side could tell the two apart, the joiner now announces its width to the store, in its own
key space rather than the scale cohort's. It announces straight after
`init_torch_distributed`, where the store first exists, because the alternative point runs
after the weights load and publishes long after the grow it has to inform.

The timing dictates the rest. The joiner is a separate process launched alongside the
scale request and cannot announce anything until it is up, measured 11s after the request
arrived and dominated by interpreter and torch import. A scheduler cannot block that long,
so it answers from a single store read: it rejects with `retry_when_joiner_announces` while
nobody has spoken and with `required_ep_size` once it knows the joiner is wider than the
target, and `_scale_elastic_ep_locked` resends on an `asyncio.sleep` until the width is
known. Every reject lands before `request_scale`, so a resend costs a round trip rather
than risking a half committed scale, and a timeout falls back to the launch width so the
previous behaviour is the floor. Neither default is safe without an announce, which is why
the wait exists at all: going direct kills a joiner wider than the target at the cohort
barrier, while assuming the launch width asks a narrower one to fill slots it has no ranks
for.

The cohort admit vote is scoped to survivors, who all count in the same width namespace,
and runs under a deadline of its own with a retry. The shrink path derives its agreement
from the retire barrier and skips the vote entirely, which keeps it out of the forward
path.

Three rendezvous read cohort state rather than lazily built local state, so every rank
answers them the same way: barrier cycle ids are seeded from the store at admission, the
NIXL retire barrier keys off
the configured backend rather than whether this rank has built its a2a buffer, and the
survivor side disconnect names only the retirees it actually connected to.

### The active ranks bitmap is converged collectively

Mooncake surfaces a transient only on the ranks whose bitmap still lags the `active_ranks`
flip, so convergence is driven from the scale finalizer as a collective: each round every
rank attempts one WORLD all-reduce and the cohort agrees the outcome over the TCPStore, so
every rank issues the same number of collectives. The round schedule is a fixed table
rather than a wall clock deadline, so two ranks reading the clock either side of one still
agree. The probe tensor is a throwaway, so reattempting is data safe, and the hot path
takes a single all-reduce.

An unplanned rank loss has no finalizer ahead of it, so nothing converges the bitmap before
the hot path resumes: the coordinator drops the dead peer on its own heartbeat timeout, and
the `mlp_sync` gather is the first collective a tick issues. A gather landing inside that
window is refused as inactive. The refusal is a precondition check raised before the
collective is posted, so no peer can have completed a gather this rank never sent, which
makes it safe to wait out where retrying a posted collective would not be. The gather now
retries only on that refusal, bounded well under the watchdog so a view that never settles
still fails loudly rather than parking the cohort. Other backends re raise unchanged.

### The fault detector stands down while the width moves

Upstream checks for faulted ranks at the tail of every forward by comparing the current
`active_ranks` against the previous one. Both tensors live on the device, so the comparison
synchronizes the stream. While a resize is in flight that sync can land on a collective a
departing or arriving peer will never post, and the cohort sees a watchdog timeout rather
than a slow tick. The fault rebalance and the NIXL mask poll both stand down until the
resize commits, which is the rule the mask poll already applied to shrinks, and the periodic
EPLB rebalance does the same so its WORLD broadcast cannot interleave with a width change.
Detection resumes on the first forward after commit, so a real fault is deferred by one
resize rather than missed.

This narrows the window rather than closing it. A few forwards still run at the new width
while a joiner compiles its first a2a kernels, because `commit_scale` clears the pending
width before the warmup phase ends. Suppressing the comparison through warmup is not the
fix: the same comparison is what triggers the post scale expert redistribution, so standing
down that long delays the rebalance and costs accuracy. Making the comparison not
synchronize needs a host side mirror that tracks Mooncake's own writes to the mask, which is
a change to upstream's fault path and is left as a follow up.

### Orchestrator facing lifecycle

- `--elastic-ep-retiree-lifecycle {self_exit,external}` selects who ends the retiree
 process. `self_exit` is the default and unchanged; `external` parks the retiree after it
 quiesces, deactivates and tears down, for an orchestrator to terminate.
- `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` reports `safe_to_terminate_ranks`, which stays empty until the
 survivors commit — a positive signal rather than an inference from a process exit.
- `/scale_elastic_ep` accepts an optional `operation_id`, echoes it, and mirrors it in
 `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` alongside the phase and `safe_to_terminate_ranks`. It is a
 correlation tag only, so the boundary is worth stating: it is not an idempotency key.
 A retried request carrying an `operation_id` already in flight is refused like any
 other concurrent resize, rather than returning or resuming the original, and the
 refusal carries `pending_ep_size` and `scale_phase` so a caller can tell a duplicate
 from a real conflict. Reusing an id with a different target is not rejected on the id.
 Joining ranks are not bound to it either. What a later resize checks is the width: the
 cohort record a joiner registers carries `target_ep_size`, and a survivor refuses the
 join when that does not match the pending target. So a stale joiner aimed at a
 different width is caught, and one aimed at the same width is not distinguished from a
 fresh one. Idempotency and join correlation identity are tracked in RFC #35376, where
 a topology generation can carry them across endpoints.
- Scale phase transitions are timestamped at `mark_phase`, the single choke point for every
 transition, so the retiring and reconfiguring phases can be attributed separately from
 the ungated drain.

### Mooncake a2a backend

The cohort barriers rendezvous over the global TCPStore, which makes the store a
requirement of the scale path itself; its creation gate now also keys off the distributed
backend, which is what decides whether the elastic FSM can run. The NIXL lanes already
satisfied the first clause, so nothing there moves.
`SGLANG_MOONCAKE_EP_BF16_DISPATCH` gives the mooncake dispatcher the same BF16 escape the
nixl dispatcher already has, defaulted off so fp8 deployments are untouched.

The rest of the shrink path needed no change for a non NIXL dispatcher: the retire barrier
keys off the a2a backend and skips, the survivor side peer disconnect no-ops without a NIXL
buffer, and the Mooncake dispatch buffer refreshes membership in place through
`update_ep_member`, which `retire_ranks` already drives.

### Compatibility

- A shrink requires a Mooncake build providing `mooncake.pg.deactivate_ranks`. Checked when
 a shrink is requested, not at init, so a Mooncake fault tolerance deployment that never
 retires a rank is not held to it and keeps booting as before. The stock 0.3.13 wheel the
 nightly image ships carries it, so no Mooncake patch is needed.
- A shrink also requires `attn_tp_size == 1` and refuses otherwise, because it reports
 retirees as DP slots (`slot_offset`/`slot_count`, `retired_ranks`, `remove_elastic_workers`
 all index workers by EP rank), which holds only while one DP slot is one EP rank. Once DP
 moves to logical replica units (`attn_tp_size > 1`, #33728) those ranges need converting
 and a shrink has to retire whole replicas; the guard makes that a clean rejection rather
 than a wrong set of deactivated workers.
- Resizing a degraded topology is refused rather than attempted. A bare fault does not
 lower `effective_ep_size`, and every cohort rendezvous sizes itself from that width, so a
 resize issued while a rank inside the width is inactive would wait on a participant that
 cannot arrive. `/scale_elastic_ep` rejects it up front, naming the inactive ranks, before
 any barrier is posted. That holds in both directions, so an `8 -> 4` whose retiring
 suffix is already short and an append grow from a degraded cohort fail the same way.
 Replacing failed capacity is the recovery path, meaning grow into the retired slots below
 the launch width, not shrink then regrow. Recovery at a nonzero launch offset, and
 retiring a set that is not the high rank suffix, both remain out of scope here.
- Bare fault recovery at launch offset 0 readmits the subgroups now, which earlier
 revisions of this PR left out of scope. A recovered rank used to get the `active_ranks`
 mask flip in every parallel group while rejoining the Mooncake process groups for WORLD
 only, so `EPBuffer.update_ep_member` all-gathered a cohort wide list into a `moe_ep`
 group that still counted survivors and raised `Tensor list size must match active group
 size`. `try_recover_faulted_ranks` joins WORLD, its sub-PGs and every live parallel
 group, which is the same set `_recover_parallel_groups` readmits a peer to. The reason
 that was held back was partial regrow, whose joiner is already active and which
 deadlocked between the survivors' `tp_cpu_group` request broadcast and the joiner's
 WORLD all-gather: partial regrow now grows direct to the target when the joiner covers
 it, so the two no longer trade off. The end to end lanes still drive the grow over NIXL,
 since only Mooncake builds that buffer and the grow collectives are NIXL only.
- The other Mooncake wide restrictions this PR adds (rejecting `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP`
 and `--enable-symm-mem`, forcing `SGLANG_USE_MESSAGE_QUEUE_BROADCASTER=False`) apply only
 when `--max-ep-size` is set, which is the opt in for a runtime scalable deployment. A
 fault tolerance only deployment logs a warning instead of failing to start, and in
 exchange it cannot shrink: `/scale_elastic_ep` refuses a scale down without
 `--max-ep-size` rather than running it on the relaxed configuration those warnings
 allowed through.
- Graph handling covers the shrink direction two ways, and composes with the decode graph
 recapture added for grow in #33723: all four of upstream's `TestElasticScaleUp*CudaGraph`
 classes pass on this tree, 3/3 each.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K is run before and after the scale in every correctness lane and asserted for parity.
Results on DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, n=128, from the certification sweep below:

| Shape | pre | post |
|---|---|---|
| 4 → 3, one node, NIXL a2a | 65.62% | 65.62% |
| 8 → 6, two nodes | 67.19% | 68.75% |
| 8 → 4, two nodes, Mooncake a2a | 65.62% | 70.31% |

Across every lane in the sweep the pre scale scores span 64.84–67.19% and the post scale
scores 64.06–68.75%, so the shrink sits inside the run to run spread of the evaluation
itself at this sample size.

`TestUnsourcedSlotsAreNotPublished` covers the weight reload contract directly: it asserts
that slots the p2p could not source are reported and left for the reload rather than
published.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V3-Lite FP8 on H100, decode graphs on against the all-eager mode elastic EP
previously used, median of 3 iterations per arm:

| | 4 → 3, one node, 8 streams | 8 → 4, two nodes, 16 streams |
|---|---|---|
| inter token latency p50 | 64.3 ms → **8.9 ms** | 65.6 ms → **8.5 ms** |
| peak stall over the shrink | 5075 ms → **13 ms** | 379 ms → **19 ms** |
| settle to the new width | 37.1 s → **4.1 s** | 34.0 s → **3.5 s** |

The 8 → 4 shape puts every retiree on the worker node, so the drain crosses the fabric
rather than resolving in one host's IPC. The lane that shrinks while a pinned decode drains
settles in 6.1 s with graphs against 69.3 s eager, since a drain bound shrink is bounded by
decode speed.

Graceful deactivation accounts for the reconfiguration itself falling from 11–12 s to under
2 s.

## Test coverage

### In CI

Thirteen CPU only files, eleven under `test/registered/unit/elastic_ep/` and two under
`test/registered/unit/eplb/`, registered with `register_cpu_ci` into `base-a-test-cpu`,
61 tests total. They need no GPU and no server,
so the pure Python contracts this PR adds are checked on every PR rather than by hand:

| File | Tests | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `test_scale_down_state_machine.py` | 11 | every FSM transition, driven through a recording stub |
| `test_scale_down_advance.py` | 5 | the per tick coordinator and the driver, with no `ModelRunner` |
| `test_store_barriers.py` | 10 | leader election, epoch reuse and round keying against a real in process `TCPStore` |
| `test_expert_map_repair.py` | 4 | orphan repair and relabel diffing, including the "increase redundancy" refusals |
| `test_elastic_stage_plan.py` | 1 | the staging plan, including which widths it splits and which it leaves for the schedulers |
| `test_append_trivial_expert_slots.py` | 2 | the expert map widening helper, and the narrowing it silently declines to do |
| `test_unsourced_expert_slots.py` | 1 | slots the p2p could not source are reported and left for the reload, not published |
| `test_fault_poll_guard.py` | 6 | the fault poll and NIXL mask poll standing down while the width is moving |
| `test_recover_group_symmetry.py` | 6 | a readmitted rank rejoining every live parallel group, not just the EP one |
| `test_drain_idle_predicate.py` | 4 | the retiree's idle predicate, so the admission gate reopens on the departing slots |
| `test_fan_out_straggler.py` | 5 | `set_fan_out` stragglers draining into the call that owns them |
| `test_gather_settle.py` | 4 | the bounded wait on Mooncake refusing an mlp_sync gather as inactive |
| `test_fail_scale_graph_recapture.py` | 2 | a failed shrink that narrowed the width requesting a decode graph rebuild |

Several files table drive their cases with `subTest`, so a row can cover more inputs than
its test count suggests.

### End to end

The multi GPU end to end cases live in the out of tree harness. The certification sweep
below covers both shapes: MC02 shrinks 4 → 3 then regrows through a recover joiner, and
MC15 shrinks while a long decode pinned to the retiring rank must return whole.

### Certification sweep

Beyond what ships here, the change is certified by a 41-lane sweep on H100,
**340 iterations, all passing, no retries,** every one reporting a GOOD log health verdict
on a single uniform tree. One lane per row, so what each one is for is visible rather than
implied.

Single node shrink, regrow and append:

| Lane | Shape | What it is for | Iter |
|---|---|---|---|
| MC01 | 4 → 3 | baseline shrink, GSM8K parity either side | 5 |
| MC02A | 4 → 3 | shrink only, NIXL a2a | 5 |
| MC02C | 4 → 3 | shrink only, Mooncake a2a. `max_ep_size == launch` leaves no recoverable slot, so upstream's NIXL only assert does not apply and the shrink is expressible | 5 |
| MC03A | 5 → 4 | shrink where every rank is a launch cohort member, so a crash isolates to the pure shrink path | 5 |
| MC04 | 4 → 3 → 2 | chained shrink; the survivor finalize starts from an already shrunk cohort | 5 |
| MC12 | 6 → 5 → 4 → 3 | three chained shrinks, crossing the retire barrier's arrival bucket boundary on cycle 3 | 5 |
| MC02 | 4 → 3 → 4 | grow back by recovering into the retired slot, over the DPC socket `remove_elastic_workers` kept bound | 5 |
| MC03 | 5 → 4 → 5 → 4 | round trip that then retires the just recovered slot | 5 |
| MC02B | launch 3, append 4 | fresh append join with headroom | 5 |
| MC03B | 4 → 5 | recover only grow after a pre shrink, in isolation | 5 |
| RECOVER | kill 4 ranks, rejoin 4 | an unplanned node loss rather than a planned shrink: the survivors readmit the dead ranks into every live parallel group, not only the EP one | 5 |
| MC14 | 4 → 3 → 4 → 5 | shrink, recover, then append, so a completed recover leaves state clean for an append | 5 |
| MC13 | 4 → 5 → 3 | append, then a shrink retiring both a launch slot and the ex append slot | 5 |

| MC21 | 4 → 2 → 3 | the same shape with a joiner sized to the target, which announces width 3 and is grown to directly. The pair that proves the planner discriminates | 10 |
| MC20 | 4 → 5 → 4 → 5 | the same append offset twice in one process, covering the group name reuse from #38503 | 5 |

Under load and over time:

|---|---|---|---|

Multi node, two 4-GPU nodes:

| Lane | Shape | What it is for | Iter |
|---|---|---|---|
| MC05 | 8 → 6 | retirees sit on the worker node; retiree exit propagates cleanly across nodes | 5 |
| MC05M | 8 → 4 | retires the entire worker node on Mooncake a2a, so the drain crosses the fabric rather than resolving in one host's IPC | 5 |
| MC08 | 8 → 4 → 8 | shrink then full regrow; the worker spawns a recover joiner for slots 4 and 5 | 5 |
| MC09 | 8 → 4 → 8 → 4 → 8 | the MC08 cycle twice in one process, so retire or recover residue leaking across the grow back shows up | 5 |
| MC10 | 8 → 4 → 8 → 6 | retires ranks the recover grow had just repopulated | 5 |

Timing bench and upstream regression:

| Lane | Shape | What it is for | Iter |
|---|---|---|---|
| BENCH_On, BENCH_Off | 4 → 3 | interruption cost with decode graphs captured, against the all-eager baseline | 6 |
| BENCH_Packed | 4 → 3 | the same with a packed EPLB layout | 3 |
| BENCH_Osl600/1k/2k | 4 → 3 | the same at 600, 1000 and 2000 output tokens | 9 |
| MNBENCH_On, MNBENCH_Off | 8 → 4 | the same measurement across nodes, graphs on and off | 6 |
| SCALEUP | 4 → 5 → 6 | upstream's append path, eager, as a regression guard | 5 |
| SCALEUPG1–4 | 4 → 5, 4 → 6, 4 → 5 → 6, 4 → 8 | upstream's append with decode graphs captured and recaptured | 12 |
| MCU | staging plan | the staging planner as a unit, no server | 1 |

Both graph modes are covered end to end: the shrink lanes and the timing bench run with
decode graphs captured, and the `SCALEUPG*` lanes run upstream's graphs on grow with
`--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16`, so the recapture on grow and preserve on shrink paths
are exercised in the same tree.

+def share_expert_map_via_store(
+    tensor: torch.Tensor, *, is_src: bool, cohort_ranks: Sequence[int], group_rank: int
+) -> bool:
+    """Hand the expert map over the store, one inbox per reader rank id (sparse after a
+    fault); False = no store. Not a broadcast (Mooncake's putTaskCuda syncs the stream)
+    nor a round keyed on participant count (desyncs when the width changes)."""
+    store = _store_or_none("[Elastic EP][expert map]")
+    if store is None or len(cohort_ranks) <= 1:
+        return False
+    if is_src:
+        blob = tensor.cpu().numpy().tobytes()
+        for peer in cohort_ranks:
+            if peer != group_rank:
+                store.set(_EXPERT_MAP_INBOX_KEY.format(peer), blob)
+        return True
+    key = _EXPERT_MAP_INBOX_KEY.format(group_rank)
+    staged = torch.frombuffer(bytearray(store.get(key)), dtype=tensor.dtype)
+    # Leave it empty so the next round blocks rather than being served this one.
+    store.delete_key(key)
+    tensor.copy_(staged.view(tensor.shape))

+@dataclass
+class _StoreBarrier:
+    """One in-flight store barrier. Its epoch is elected: arrival 1 mints the next cycle
+    id and later arrivals read it, so chained scales cannot share a key."""
+
+    ns: str
+    rank: int
+    epoch: int
+    world_size: int
+    ready_key: str
+    arrival: int = 0
+    posted_at: float = 0.0
+    first_check: bool = True
+    last_poll: float = 0.0
+
+    @property
+    def tag(self) -> str:
+        return _BARRIER_NS[self.ns][3]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def post(
+        cls, store, rank: int, ns: str, target: int, *, rewind_on_fail: bool = False
+    ) -> Optional[_StoreBarrier]:
+        """Elect an epoch, then announce on its ready key. ``rewind_on_fail`` frees a
+        leader's epoch on a failed announce (a sync driver must not reuse one)."""
+        epoch, arrival = cls._elect_epoch(store, rank, ns)
+        if epoch is None:
+            return None
+        ready_key = _BARRIER_NS[ns][2].format(epoch)
+        try:
+            store.add(ready_key, 1)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            logger.warning(
+                "%s rank=%d ready_key add fail e=%d (%s)",
+                _BARRIER_NS[ns][3],
+                rank,
+                epoch,
+                exc,
+            )
+            if rewind_on_fail and arrival == 1:
+                with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
+                    store.add(_BARRIER_NS[ns][1], -1)
+                _last_local_cycle_id[ns] = epoch - 1
+            # Always unwind: ARRIVAL must return to a base where a later cycle reads 1.
+            cls._unwind(store, rank, ns)
+            return None
+        return cls(ns, rank, epoch, target, ready_key, arrival, time.monotonic())
+
+    def check(self, store, secs: float) -> tuple[bool, int]:
+        """Poll until target or ``secs`` (0 = one probe); returns (reached, count)."""
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + secs
+        seen = 0
+        while True:
+            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
+                seen = _store_int(store, self.ready_key)
+                if seen >= self.world_size:
+                    return True, seen
+            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+                return False, seen
+            time.sleep(_BARRIER_STORE_POLL_S)
+
+    def consume(self) -> None:
+        """Leader-only ARRIVAL reset, so the next cycle's first arrival reads 1 again.
+        Warned, not swallowed: a counter left high costs elasticity for the process."""
+        if self.arrival != 1:
+            return
+        try:
+            store = get_global_tcp_store()
+            if store is not None:
+                store.set(_BARRIER_NS[self.ns][0], "0")
+        except Exception as exc:
+            logger.warning(
+                "%s rank=%d ARRIVAL reset failed e=%d (%s)",
+                self.tag,
+                self.rank,
+                self.epoch,
+                exc,
+            )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _unwind(store, rank: int, ns: str) -> None:
+        """Undo this arrival. Decrement: set(0) stomps peers, minting a 2nd leader."""
+        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
+            store.add(_BARRIER_NS[ns][0], -1)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _elect_epoch(cls, store, rank: int, ns: str) -> tuple[Optional[int], int]:
+        """arrival 1 = leader and mints the cycle id, >=2 = follower and reads it.
+        On epoch=None our ARRIVAL is already unwound; the caller only falls back."""
+        arrival_key, cycle_key, _, log = _BARRIER_NS[ns]
+        try:
+            arrival = int(store.add(arrival_key, 1))
+        except Exception as exc:
+            logger.warning("%s rank=%d arrival add failed (%s)", log, rank, exc)
+            return None, 0
+        if arrival == 1:
+            try:
+                epoch = int(store.add(cycle_key, 1))
+                _last_local_cycle_id[ns] = epoch
+                return epoch, arrival
+            except Exception as exc:
+                logger.warning("%s rank=%d cycle add failed (%s)", log, rank, exc)
+        else:
+            prev = _last_local_cycle_id[ns]
+            deadline = time.monotonic() + _BARRIER_EPOCH_CATCH_UP_S
+            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
+                try:
+                    candidate = _store_int(store, cycle_key)
+                except Exception:
+                    candidate = prev
+                if candidate > prev:
+                    _last_local_cycle_id[ns] = candidate
+                    return candidate, arrival
+                time.sleep(_BARRIER_STORE_POLL_S)
+            logger.warning("%s rank=%d arrival=%d cycle id timeout", log, rank, arrival)
+        cls._unwind(store, rank, ns)
+        return None, arrival
+

+_BarrierHandle = Union[_StoreBarrier, _BarrierSkip, None]

+def retire_barrier_check(
+    state: _BarrierHandle,
+    *,
+    block_s: Optional[float] = None,
+    keep_serving: bool = False,
+) -> bool:
+    """Non-blocking probe: True when every cohort rank posted. TimeoutError at 300s.
+    ``block_s`` waits in place, for a caller that must not re-enter the event loop.
+    ``keep_serving`` skips the catch-up window, which would stall a serving cohort."""
+    if isinstance(state, _BarrierSkip):
+        return True
+    if state is None:
+        return False  # post failed: fail closed so the FSM re-posts
+    store = _store_or_none()
+    seen = "no store"
+    if store is not None:
+        now = time.monotonic()
+        # One catch-up window, then non-blocking polls: sleeping per tick slows decode.
+        if block_s is not None:
+            window = block_s
+        elif state.first_check and not keep_serving:
+            state.first_check = False
+            window = _BARRIER_EPOCH_CATCH_UP_S
+        elif now - state.last_poll < _BARRIER_RECHECK_S:
+            return False
+        else:
+            window = 0.0
+        state.last_poll = now
+        reached, seen = state.check(store, window)
+        if reached:
+            return True
+
+    if time.monotonic() - state.posted_at > _RETIRE_BARRIER_TIMEOUT_S:
+        # Hand ARRIVAL back before giving up, or no later cycle can elect a leader.
+        state.consume()
+        raise TimeoutError(
+            f"{state.tag} rank={state.rank} e={state.epoch} timeout "
+            f"{seen}/{state.world_size} @ {_RETIRE_BARRIER_TIMEOUT_S:.0f}s"
+        )
+    return False
+

+def retire_barrier_consume(state: _BarrierHandle) -> None:
+    """Finalize the barrier; only the leader resets ARRIVAL_KEY."""
+    if isinstance(state, _StoreBarrier):
+        state.consume()

+_departure_announced_at: Optional[float] = None
+_departure_cleared = False
+# Backstop for a gather not carrying the flag, where a staggered exit beats a hang.
+_DEPARTURE_ALIGN_BUDGET_S = 30.0
+
+
+def departure_announce() -> None:
+    """Declare this rank done with DRAIN. Idempotent: the deadline is set once."""
+    global _departure_announced_at
+    if _departure_announced_at is None:
+        _departure_announced_at = time.monotonic()
+
+
+def departure_pending() -> bool:
+    """Our mlp_sync gather element: True while this rank still holds the cohort."""
+    return _departure_announced_at is None
+
+
+def departure_observe(cleared: bool) -> None:
+    """Record the gather's verdict. Called from the mlp_sync, once per iteration."""
+    global _departure_cleared
+    _departure_cleared = cleared
+
+
+def departure_cleared() -> bool:
+    if _departure_cleared:
+        return True
+    if _departure_announced_at is None:
+        return False
+    if time.monotonic() - _departure_announced_at < _DEPARTURE_ALIGN_BUDGET_S:
+        return False
+    logger.warning(
+        "[Elastic EP] departing DRAIN unaligned after %.0fs: the mlp_sync gather never "
+        "reported cohort readiness, so peers may still be in the serving loop",
+        _DEPARTURE_ALIGN_BUDGET_S,
+    )
+    return True
+
+
+def departure_reset() -> None:
+    global _departure_announced_at, _departure_cleared
+    _departure_announced_at = None
+    _departure_cleared = False
+
+
+def retire_barrier_post() -> _BarrierHandle:
+    """Post the WORLD retire barrier. BARRIER_SKIP = nothing to sync; None = post
+    failed, caller must retry. Over the store, not a collective: Mooncake issues each
+    behind the previous one's completion; one pending across ticks stalls mlp_sync."""
+    if not torch.distributed.is_initialized():
+        return BARRIER_SKIP
+    return _post_retire_barrier("world")
+
+
+def retiree_local_cleanup() -> None:
+    """CUDA quiesce, deactivate, then tear the backends down, all before sys.exit(0)."""
+    if torch.cuda.is_available():
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+    # Last Mooncake call: no tick follows, so nothing broadcasts once we are dropped.
+    _mooncake_deactivate_self()
+    _destroy_local_process_groups()
+
+
+def _destroy_local_process_groups() -> None:
+    """Tear down our backends now, not at exit, where Mooncake's destructors would hit
+    an unloading CUDA driver and std::terminate all survivors. Subgroups first."""
+    seen = {id(torch.distributed.group.WORLD)}
+    groups = []
+    for group in _iter_live_parallel_groups():
+        for pg in (group.device_group, group.cpu_group):
+            if pg is not None and id(pg) not in seen:
+                seen.add(id(pg))
+                groups.append((group.unique_name, pg))
+    for label, pg in groups + [("WORLD", None)]:
+        try:
+            torch.distributed.destroy_process_group(pg)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            logger.warning("[Elastic EP][retire] destroy %s failed: %s", label, exc)

+"""Expert-map repair for an elastic shrink. Survivors repair independently without
+exchanging maps, so the rule must be deterministic."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Callable, Dict, List
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.errors import ElasticLayoutFatal
+from sglang.srt.eplb.expert_location import (
+    ExpertLocationMetadata,
+    get_global_expert_location_metadata,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def local_relabelled_logicals(
+    old_p2l: torch.Tensor,
+    new_p2l: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    num_local: int,
+    ep_rank: int,
+) -> Dict[int, List[int]]:
+    """Per layer, logicals this rank's own slots now hold but did not before; slots
+    past the old width count as changed."""
+    lo = num_local * ep_rank
+    hi = min(lo + num_local, new_p2l.shape[1])
+    if hi <= lo:
+        return {}
+    window = new_p2l[:, lo:hi]
+    changed = torch.ones_like(window, dtype=torch.bool)
+    overlap = min(old_p2l.shape[1], hi) - lo
+    if overlap > 0:
+        changed[:, :overlap] = window[:, :overlap] != old_p2l[:, lo : lo + overlap]
+    changed &= window >= 0
+    return {
+        layer_id: sorted(set(logicals))
+        for layer_id in range(window.shape[0])
+        if (logicals := window[layer_id][changed[layer_id]].tolist())
+    }
+
+
+def repair_orphan_logicals(
+    *, shrunk_p2l: torch.Tensor, num_logical: int
+) -> Dict[int, List[int]]:
+    """Give every logical a replica by relabelling duplicated slots of ``shrunk_p2l``
+    in place. Returns the relabelled logicals per layer; the caller must reload them."""
+    num_layers, new_num_physical = shrunk_p2l.shape
+    if new_num_physical < num_logical:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Shrink leaves {new_num_physical} slots for {num_logical} logicals; "
+            "increase --ep-num-redundant-experts."
+        )
+
+    # Keyed by the global layer id the weight-name filter parses.
+    repaired: Dict[int, List[int]] = {}
+    for layer_id in range(num_layers):
+        row = shrunk_p2l[layer_id].tolist()
+        counts = [0] * num_logical
+        for value in row:
+            if 0 <= value < num_logical:
+                counts[value] += 1
+        orphans = [l for l in range(num_logical) if counts[l] == 0]
+        if not orphans:
+            continue
+        repaired[layer_id] = orphans
+        for orphan in orphans:
+            for slot_idx, value in enumerate(row):
+                if 0 <= value < num_logical and counts[value] >= 2:
+                    counts[value] -= 1
+                    row[slot_idx] = orphan
+                    counts[orphan] = 1
+                    break
+            else:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"Layer {layer_id}: no duplicate to cover logical {orphan}; "
+                    "increase --ep-num-redundant-experts."
+                )
+        shrunk_p2l[layer_id] = torch.tensor(
+            row, dtype=shrunk_p2l.dtype, device=shrunk_p2l.device
+        )
+
+    if repaired:
+        logger.warning(
+            "[Elastic EP] shrink orphaned %d logical expert(s) across %d layer(s); "
+            "reloading their weights (the donor slots hold the wrong ones): %s",
+            sum(len(v) for v in repaired.values()),
+            len(repaired),
+            dict(list(repaired.items())[:4]),
+        )
+    return repaired
+
+
+def shrink_expert_metadata(
+    *,
+    model_config: ModelConfig,
+    from_ep_size: int,
+    effective_size: int,
+    moe_ep_rank: int,
+    reload_relabelled: Callable[[Dict[int, List[int]]], None],
+) -> None:
+    """Truncate physical_to_logical_map to survivor slots + repair orphaned logicals."""
+    metadata = get_global_expert_location_metadata()
+    if metadata is None:
+        return
+    old_num_physical = metadata.num_physical_experts
+    new_num_physical = old_num_physical // from_ep_size * effective_size
+    if new_num_physical >= old_num_physical:
+        return
+
+    get_context().override("elastic_ep.scale", ep_size=effective_size)
+    # clone(), not contiguous(): a single-MoE-layer slice is already contiguous, so
+    # the repair below would write through into the still-installed metadata.
+    shrunk_p2l = metadata.physical_to_logical_map[:, :new_num_physical].clone()
+    relabelled = repair_orphan_logicals(
+        shrunk_p2l=shrunk_p2l, num_logical=metadata.num_logical_experts
+    )
+    metadata.adopt_scaled_in_place(
+        ExpertLocationMetadata.init_by_mapping(
+            model_config, physical_to_logical_map=shrunk_p2l, moe_ep_rank=moe_ep_rank
+        )
+    )
+    # After install so the loader follows the map. Fatal on failure: the map says a
+    # slot holds the orphan while it still holds its donor.
+    try:
+        reload_relabelled(relabelled)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise ElasticLayoutFatal(
+            "Elastic EP shrink left this rank's expert weights out of sync with "
+            f"its expert map ({exc}). It must not continue serving."
+        ) from exc

+"""Adapter from ``ScaleDownStateMachine`` transitions to their side effects; the two
+runner-owned tails arrive as callables, so tests can drive the machine with a stub."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import time
+from typing import Callable, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.elastic_ep import (
+    ElasticEPStateManager,
+    _pre_nixl_retire,
+    departure_announce,
+    departure_cleared,
+    departure_reset,
+    nixl_retire_barrier_post,
+    retire_barrier_check,
+    retire_barrier_consume,
+    retire_barrier_post,
+    retiree_local_cleanup,
+    try_retire_ranks,
+)
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.scale_down_state import ScaleDownStateMachine
+
+
+class ScaleDownDriver:
+    """FSM driver: bridges state transitions to the side effects they need."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, finalize_scale_down: Callable, retire_and_exit: Callable, is_idle=None
+    ) -> None:
+        self._finalize_scale_down = finalize_scale_down
+        self._retire_and_exit = retire_and_exit
+        self._is_idle = is_idle
+
+    def on_prepare(self, sm):
+        departure_reset()
+        ElasticEPStateManager.mark_phase("draining")
+
+    def local_idle(self, sm) -> bool:
+        """No local work left; unwired reads idle rather than hold the cohort."""
+        return self._is_idle is None or self._is_idle()
+
+    def post_drain_barrier(self, sm):
+        return retire_barrier_post()
+
+    def announce_departure(self, sm):
+        departure_announce()
+
+    def departure_cleared(self, sm) -> bool:
+        return departure_cleared()
+
+    def on_depart_drain(self, sm):
+        ElasticEPStateManager.mark_phase("retiring")
+
+    def check_barrier(self, handle, *, block_s=None, keep_serving=False):
+        return retire_barrier_check(handle, block_s=block_s, keep_serving=keep_serving)
+
+    def consume_barrier(self, handle):
+        retire_barrier_consume(handle)
+
+    def on_retiree_quiesce(self, sm):
+        # FLIP_MASK narrows the device-side expert bound in-flight a2a asserts on, and
+        # is_fully_idle() gates the scheduler, not the device.
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    def on_nixl_retire_pre(self, sm):
+        # Quiesce while both peers are connected: the barrier posts a tick early so a2a
+        # keeps queueing, and disconnecting over in-flight RDMA spins forever.
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        _pre_nixl_retire(sm.ranks_to_retire)
+
+    def post_nixl_retire_barrier(self, sm):
+        return nixl_retire_barrier_post()
+
+    def on_flip_mask(self, sm):
+        try_retire_ranks(sm.ranks_to_retire)
+
+    def on_reconfig(self, sm):
+        self._finalize_scale_down(
+            ranks_to_retire=sm.ranks_to_retire,
+            target_size=sm.target_size,
+            effective_size=sm.effective_size,
+        )
+
+    def on_local_cleanup(self, sm):
+        retiree_local_cleanup()
+
+    def on_exit(self, sm):
+        self._retire_and_exit()
+
+
+def advance_scale_down(
+    *,
+    sm: Optional[ScaleDownStateMachine],
+    driver: ScaleDownDriver,
+    pending_size: int,
+    effective_size: int,
+    pending_since: float,
+    my_global_rank: int,
+    scale_timeout: float,
+    fail_scale: Callable[[str, int], None],
+) -> Optional[ScaleDownStateMachine]:
+    """Step the shrink one tick; returns the machine to keep, or None once terminal."""
+    if time.monotonic() - pending_since > scale_timeout:
+        fail_scale(
+            f"Timed out waiting for cohort at retire barrier (target={pending_size})",
+            effective_size,
+        )
+        if sm is not None:
+            sm.abandon(driver)
+        return None
+
+    if sm is None:
+        ranks_to_retire = list(range(pending_size, effective_size))
+        sm = ScaleDownStateMachine(
+            is_retiree=my_global_rank in ranks_to_retire,
+            target_size=pending_size,
+            effective_size=effective_size,
+            ranks_to_retire=ranks_to_retire,
+            my_global_rank=my_global_rank,
+        )
+
+    sm.tick(driver)
+    if sm.is_failed():
+        fail_scale(sm.last_error or "unknown scale-down FSM failure", effective_size)
+        sm.abandon(driver)
+    return None if sm.is_terminal() else sm

+keyword and the result says what the runner should write, so fakes can stand in."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import sys
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Callable, Dict, List, NoReturn, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.elastic_ep import (
+    ElasticEPStateManager,
+    await_retirees_departed,
+)
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.expert_map_repair import shrink_expert_metadata
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.eplb.eplb_manager import ExpertLayoutDivergence
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_exec
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig
+    from sglang.srt.eplb.eplb_manager import EPLBManager
+    from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import ElasticScaleUpdateReq
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScaleDownFinalizeResult:
+    """What the survivor tail asks ModelRunner to write once it returns."""
+
+    request_graph_recapture: bool = False
+    scale_update: Optional[ElasticScaleUpdateReq] = None
+
+
+def retire_and_exit(
+    *, my_global_rank: int, park_hook: Optional[Callable[[], None]]
+) -> NoReturn:
+    """Retiree terminal: exit, or park for an orchestrator. FSM EXIT after cleanup."""
+    if get_exec().moe.elastic_ep_retiree_lifecycle == "external":
+        # Never return: the caller's event loop would collect on destroyed groups.
+        logger.info(
+            "[Elastic EP][retire] rank=%d parked; awaiting external termination",
+            my_global_rank,
+        )
+        # The scheduler's hook disarms its watchdog, which would otherwise SIGQUIT
+        # the parent; the loop alone covers a runner with no scheduler behind it.
+        if park_hook is not None:
+            park_hook()
+        while True:
+            time.sleep(5.0)
+    sys.exit(0)
+
+
+def finalize_scale_down(
+    *,
+    model_config: ModelConfig,
+    moe_ep_rank: int,
+    eplb: Optional[EPLBManager],
+    reload_relabelled: Callable[[Dict[int, List[int]]], None],
+    apply_dp_size: Callable[[int, int], None],
+    scale_ready_barrier: Callable[..., None],
+    init_lplb_solvers: Callable[[], None],
+    reinit_recorder: Callable[..., None],
+    rearm_eplb: Callable[[], None],
+    ranks_to_retire: List[int],
+    target_size: int,
+    effective_size: int,

+    from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import ElasticScaleUpdateReq

+    await_retirees_departed(ranks_to_retire)
+    ElasticEPStateManager.mark_phase("reconfiguring")

+        eplb.reset_generator()
+        # Before the truncation below, which rewrites the map the recorder converts
+        # through; the reshuffle further down is what consumes these counts.
+        logical_count = eplb.snapshot_logical_count()
+
+    # No broadcast: every survivor repairs the same pre-shrink map by the same rule.
+    shrink_expert_metadata(
+        model_config=model_config,
+        from_ep_size=effective_size,
+        effective_size=target_size,
+        moe_ep_rank=moe_ep_rank,
+        reload_relabelled=reload_relabelled,

+    ElasticEPStateManager.mark_syncing_new_world()

+    if reuse_graphs:

+            "[Elastic EP] keeping decode CUDA graphs across %d -> %d",
+            effective_size,
+            target_size,
+        )

+        request_graph_recapture=not reuse_graphs, scale_update=scale_update
+    )

+"""Mooncake-native scale-down state machine, advanced one stage per scheduler tick.
+Barriers poll the TCPStore across ticks so a waiting rank keeps servicing mlp_sync."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum, auto
+from typing import Any, List, Optional
+
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.errors import ElasticLayoutFatal
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class ScaleDownState(Enum):
+    PREPARE = auto()
+    DRAIN = auto()
+    NIXL_RETIRE = auto()
+    FLIP_MASK = auto()
+    RECONFIG = auto()  # survivor-only
+    COMPLETE = auto()  # survivor terminal
+    LOCAL_CLEANUP = auto()  # retiree-only
+    EXIT = auto()  # retiree terminal
+    FAILED = auto()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ScaleDownStateMachine:
+    """Per-rank scale-down driver owned by ModelRunner; torn down at terminal."""
+
+    is_retiree: bool
+    target_size: int
+    effective_size: int
+    ranks_to_retire: List[int]
+    my_global_rank: int
+    state: ScaleDownState = ScaleDownState.PREPARE
+    last_error: Optional[str] = None
+    _drain_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _drain_post_attempts: int = 0
+    _drain_barrier_done: bool = False
+    _departure_announced: bool = False
+    _nixl_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _nixl_post_attempts: int = 0
+    # Bounded re-arms, then fail rather than flip the mask unsynchronized.
+    BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS: int = 20
+    # Under the barrier's own 300s timeout, so an absent peer is reported there.
+    RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S: float = 120.0
+
+    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
+        S = ScaleDownState
+        return self.state in (S.COMPLETE, S.EXIT, S.FAILED)
+
+    def abandon(self, driver) -> None:
+        """Release any posted barrier. Idempotent. The epoch leader owes the ARRIVAL
+        reset; leaking it wedges every later scale."""
+        for attr in ("_drain_barrier_handle", "_nixl_barrier_handle"):
+            handle = getattr(self, attr)
+            if handle is None:
+                continue
+            setattr(self, attr, None)
+            try:
+                driver.consume_barrier(handle)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "[Elastic EP] releasing %s during teardown failed",
+                    attr,
+                    exc_info=True,
+                )
+
+    def is_failed(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state is ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def tick(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        """Advance by one stage per call. Side effects live in driver callbacks."""
+        if self.is_terminal():
+            return
+        try:
+            self._advance(driver)
+            if self.state is ScaleDownState.EXIT:
+                driver.on_exit(self)
+        except ElasticLayoutFatal:
+            # Not FAILED: that keeps serving, and this rank's map and weights disagree.
+            raise
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+            logger.error(
+                "[Elastic EP][scale-down FSM] rank=%d %s failed in %s",
+                self.my_global_rank,
+                "retiree" if self.is_retiree else "survivor",
+                self.state.name.lower(),
+                exc_info=True,
+            )
+            self.state = ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def _fold_nixl_to_flip(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        # Post once per cycle: re-posting double-counts arrivals and lets a subset pass.
+        if self._nixl_barrier_handle is None:
+            self._nixl_post_attempts += 1
+            if self._nixl_post_attempts > self.BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"NIXL retire barrier failed to arm after "
+                    f"{self._nixl_post_attempts - 1} attempts"
+                )
+            self._nixl_barrier_handle = driver.post_nixl_retire_barrier(self)
+        # A retiree blocks rather than polls: re-ticking would post a collective
+        # against peers already in reconfig.
+        if not driver.check_barrier(
+            self._nixl_barrier_handle,
+            block_s=self.RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S if self.is_retiree else None,
+        ):
+            return

+IDLE = SimpleNamespace(is_empty=lambda: True)
+BUSY = SimpleNamespace(is_empty=lambda: False)
+
+
+def _gate(*, closed, retiring):
+    event = asyncio.Event()
+    if not closed:
+        event.set()
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        _elastic_shrink_pause_event=event, _elastic_shrink_retiring=set(retiring)
+    )

+
+class TestPendingResults(CustomTestCase):
+    CASES = [
+        # (case, batches, ignore_idle_batches, expected)
+        ("strict count includes idle batches", (IDLE, BUSY), False, 2),
+        ("idle batches discounted", (IDLE, BUSY), True, 1),
+        ("all idle reads as drained", (IDLE,) * 4, True, 0),
+        ("all idle, strict", (IDLE,) * 4, False, 4),
+        ("real work still blocks", (BUSY,), True, 1),
+        ("empty queue, strict", (), False, 0),
+        ("empty queue, discounted", (), True, 0),
+    ]
+
+    def test_pending_results(self):
+        for case, batches, ignore, expected in self.CASES:
+            with self.subTest(case):
+                sched = SimpleNamespace(result_queue=[(b, object()) for b in batches])
+                self.assertEqual(Scheduler._pending_results(sched, ignore), expected)
+
+
+class TestShrinkGateScope(CustomTestCase):
+    """Only a pin onto a departing slot waits. Everything else goes through."""
+
+    CASES = [
+        # (case, closed, retiring, request, admitted)
+        ("open gate admits everything", False, (1, 2), {"routed_dp_rank": 1}, True),
+        ("closed gate admits unpinned", True, (1, 2), {"routed_dp_rank": None}, True),
+        ("closed gate admits a live pin", True, (2, 3), {"routed_dp_rank": 0}, True),
+        ("closed gate holds retiring pin", True, (2, 3), {"routed_dp_rank": 3}, False),
+        ("no pin attribute is admitted", True, (1, 2), {}, True),
+    ]
+
+    def test_gate_scope(self):
+        for case, closed, retiring, request, admitted in self.CASES:
+            with self.subTest(case):
+                tm = _gate(closed=closed, retiring=retiring)
+                wait = TokenizerManager._await_elastic_shrink_gate(
+                    tm, SimpleNamespace(**request)
+                )
+                loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
+                try:
+                    loop.run_until_complete(asyncio.wait_for(wait, 0.05))
+                    got = True

+"""A shrink that fails after the mask flip must rebuild decode graphs captured wider."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+from sglang.srt.model_executor import model_runner as model_runner_module
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.model_runner import ModelRunner
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci

+
+LAUNCH_WIDTH = 4
+
+
+def _fail_scale(live_width, has_decode_graph=True):
+    """Fail a scale on a runner captured at LAUNCH_WIDTH; True if it asks to rebuild."""
+    runner = ModelRunner.__new__(ModelRunner)
+    runner._elastic_pending_graph_recapture = False
+    graph = SimpleNamespace(num_dp_ranks=LAUNCH_WIDTH) if has_decode_graph else None
+    runner.decode_cuda_graph_runner = graph
+    runner._reset_eplb_after_elastic_scale_failure = lambda: None
+    # The width the failure leaves behind comes from the patched get_parallel().
+    runner._narrow_to_reconciled_width = lambda reconciled: None
+    runner._report_elastic_scale_failure = lambda error, size: None
+    runner._elastic_global_rank = lambda: 1  # non-zero: rank 0 only adds a log line
+    state = mock.Mock(spec=["fail_scale", "get_effective_ep_size"])
+    state.get_effective_ep_size.return_value = live_width
+    parallel = SimpleNamespace(num_dp_ranks=live_width)
+    with (
+        mock.patch.object(model_runner_module, "ElasticEPStateManager", state),
+        mock.patch.object(model_runner_module, "get_parallel", lambda: parallel),
+    ):
+        runner._fail_scale("scale failed", live_width)
+    # The recapture request is additive: it must not displace the report.
+    state.fail_scale.assert_called_once_with("scale failed")
+    return runner._elastic_pending_graph_recapture
+

+class TestFailScaleGraphRecapture(unittest.TestCase):

+"""A reply owed to a call ``set_fan_out`` cut short must not reach the next call."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+import asyncio
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.managers.communicator import FanOutCommunicator
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+LAUNCH_FAN_OUT = 4
+
+
+def _comm(send=lambda obj: None):
+    return FanOutCommunicator(send=send, fan_out=LAUNCH_FAN_OUT, mode="queueing")
+
+
+async def _call(comm, obj, replies):
+    """Start a call and feed it ``replies``: ints, which like ReqOutput carry no id."""
+    call = asyncio.ensure_future(comm(obj))
+    await asyncio.sleep(0)
+    for reply in replies:
+        comm.handle_recv(reply)
+    return call
+
+
+class TestFanOutStraggler(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_two_sequential_calls_stay_separate(self):
+        """set_fan_out is only called by a resize, so the drain must be unreachable."""
+
+        async def body():
+            comm, results = _comm(), []
+            for base in (0, 10):
+                call = await _call(comm, "req", range(base, base + LAUNCH_FAN_OUT))
+                results.append(await asyncio.wait_for(call, timeout=1.0))
+            return results
+
+        self.assertEqual(asyncio.run(body()), [[0, 1, 2, 3], [10, 11, 12, 13]])
+
+    def test_straggler_is_absorbed_not_handed_to_the_next_call(self):
+        """The leak itself; without the drain the next call returns [99, 10, 11, 12]."""
+
+        async def body():
+            comm = _comm()
+            first = await _call(comm, "a", range(3))
+            asyncio.get_running_loop().call_later(0.01, comm.handle_recv, 99)
+            # Queued on the lock before the first call finishes, which is what puts
+            # its bucket in the straggler's path.
+            second = asyncio.ensure_future(comm("b"))
+            comm.set_fan_out(3)
+            first_out = await asyncio.wait_for(first, timeout=3.0)
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
+            for i in range(3):
+                comm.handle_recv(10 + i)
+            return first_out, await asyncio.wait_for(second, timeout=3.0)
+
+        self.assertEqual(asyncio.run(body()), ([0, 1, 2], [10, 11, 12]))
+
+    def test_a_straggler_that_never_arrives_is_bounded(self):
+        """A retiree that exited without answering must not hold the lock open."""
+
+        async def body():
+            comm = _comm()
+            call = await _call(comm, "req", range(3))
+            comm.set_fan_out(3)
+            loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+            started = loop.time()
+            out = await asyncio.wait_for(call, timeout=2.0)
+            return out, loop.time() - started
+
+        out, elapsed = asyncio.run(body())
+        self.assertEqual(out, [0, 1, 2])
+        self.assertLess(elapsed, 1.0)
+
+    def test_the_next_call_still_runs_after_a_short_one(self):
+        sent = []
+
+        async def body():
+            comm = _comm(sent.append)
+            first = await _call(comm, "a", range(3))
+            comm.set_fan_out(3)
+            await asyncio.wait_for(first, timeout=2.0)
+            second = await _call(comm, "b", range(20, 23))
+            return await asyncio.wait_for(second, timeout=2.0)
+
+        self.assertEqual(asyncio.run(body()), [20, 21, 22])
+        self.assertEqual(sent, ["a", "b"])
+
+    def test_cancelled_caller_does_not_poison_the_next_call(self):
+        async def body():
+            comm = _comm()
+            call = await _call(comm, "req", [0])
+            call.cancel()
+            with self.assertRaises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+                await call
+            second = await _call(comm, "req", range(30, 34))
+            return await asyncio.wait_for(second, timeout=1.0)
+
+        self.assertEqual(asyncio.run(body()), [30, 31, 32, 33])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+import sys

+
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+WORLD_SIZE = 4
+FAULTED_RANK = 2
+
+
+class FakePg:
+    def __init__(self, label):
+        self.label = label
+
+
+class FakeGroup:
+    """The parts of GroupCoordinator the recover and join paths read."""
+
+    def __init__(self, name, ranks):
+        self.unique_name = name
+        self.ranks = list(ranks)
+        self.world_size = len(ranks)
+        self.device_group = FakePg(f"{name}.device")
+        self.cpu_group = FakePg(f"{name}.cpu")

+        self.mq_broadcaster = None
+
+
+class RecordingMooncake(types.ModuleType):
+    """Stands in for ``mooncake.pg`` and records which PGs each side touched."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__("mooncake.pg")
+        self.recovered, self.joined, self.peer_state_ok = [], [], True
+
+    def recover_ranks(self, pg, ranks):
+        self.recovered.append((pg.label, tuple(ranks)))
+
+    def join_group(self, pg):
+        self.joined.append(pg.label)
+
+    def get_peer_state(self, pg, ranks):

+
+    def deactivate_ranks(self, pg, ranks):

+        )

+        self.solo = FakeGroup("solo:0", [FAULTED_RANK])

+        self.mooncake = RecordingMooncake()
+        self.default_pg = FakePg("default_world")
+        modules = {
+            "mooncake": types.ModuleType("mooncake"),

+        ):

+            self.addCleanup(patch.stop)

+    def sub_group_labels(self):
+        """Every non-WORLD PG a shrink would have deactivated for the faulted rank."""
+        return {

+RETIREE_RANK = 3
+SURVIVOR_RANK = 0
+
+
+def advance(sm, driver, failures=None, *, timed_out=False):
+    failures = [] if failures is None else failures
+    return advance_scale_down(
+        sm=sm,
+        driver=driver,
+        pending_size=PENDING_SIZE,
+        effective_size=EFFECTIVE_SIZE,
+        pending_since=0.0 if timed_out else time.monotonic(),
+        my_global_rank=SURVIVOR_RANK,

+    )

+class TestAdvanceScaleDown(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_hands_back_the_same_machine_until_it_is_terminal(self):
+        driver = RecordingDriver()
+        sm = advance(None, driver)
+        # Retiring the tail slots is derived from the width pair, not passed in.
+        self.assertEqual(sm.ranks_to_retire, [RETIREE_RANK])
+        self.assertFalse(sm.is_retiree)
+        for _ in range(20):
+            nxt = advance(sm, driver)
+            if nxt is None:
+                break
+            self.assertIs(nxt, sm)
+        # None means the caller drops it, and the survivor got its reconfig.
+        self.assertIsNone(nxt)
+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.COMPLETE)
+        self.assertIn("on_reconfig", driver.calls)

+        driver, failures = RecordingDriver(barrier_ready=False), []
+        sm = advance(None, driver)

+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.DRAIN)
+        self.assertEqual(driver.consumed, [])
+        self.assertIsNone(advance(sm, driver, failures, timed_out=True))
+        self.assertEqual(len(failures), 1)
+        self.assertIn("retire barrier", failures[0])
+        # Abandoned, not leaked: the epoch this rank posted is reset.
+        self.assertEqual(len(driver.consumed), 1)
+
+    def test_a_failure_before_any_machine_exists_still_fails_the_scale(self):
+        """A timeout, or a driver exception: FAILED is terminal, so dropped at once."""
+        failing = RecordingDriver()
+        failing.on_prepare = Mock(side_effect=RuntimeError("prepare blew up"))
+        for driver, timed_out, error in (
+            (RecordingDriver(), True, "retire barrier"),
+            (failing, False, "prepare blew up"),
+        ):

+                failures = []
+                self.assertIsNone(advance(None, driver, failures, timed_out=timed_out))

+                self.assertIn(error, failures[0])

+"""Unit tests for the elastic scale-down FSM, driven through a recording driver stub."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import Mock
+
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.scale_down_state import (
+    ScaleDownState,
+    ScaleDownStateMachine,
+)
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+from _fakes import RecordingDriver  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def make_sm(is_retiree):
+    return ScaleDownStateMachine(
+        is_retiree=is_retiree,
+        target_size=3,
+        effective_size=4,
+        ranks_to_retire=[3],
+        my_global_rank=3 if is_retiree else 0,
+    )
+
+
+def run(sm, driver, max_ticks=20):
+    """Tick until terminal, at most ``max_ticks`` times."""
+    for _ in range(max_ticks):
+        if sm.is_terminal():
+            return
+        sm.tick(driver)
+
+
+class TestScaleDownStateMachine(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_survivor_flips_after_the_nixl_barrier_and_reconfigures(self):
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=False), RecordingDriver()
+        run(sm, driver)
+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.COMPLETE)
+        calls = list(driver.calls)
+        # The flip narrows the device-side expert bound, so every peer must have
+        # crossed the NIXL barrier before it happens.
+        self.assertLess(
+            calls.index("post_nixl_retire_barrier"), calls.index("on_flip_mask")
+        )
+        self.assertLess(calls.index("on_flip_mask"), calls.index("on_reconfig"))
+        self.assertEqual(calls.count("announce_departure"), 1)
+        # A survivor never runs retiree-only side effects.
+        self.assertNotIn("on_local_cleanup", calls)
+        self.assertNotIn("on_exit", calls)
+        sm.tick(driver)  # a terminal state ignores further ticks
+        self.assertEqual(driver.calls, calls)
+
+    def test_retiree_reaches_exit_after_cleanup(self):
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=True), RecordingDriver()
+        run(sm, driver)
+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.EXIT)
+        self.assertLess(
+            driver.calls.index("on_local_cleanup"), driver.calls.index("on_exit")
+        )
+        self.assertNotIn("on_reconfig", driver.calls)
+
+    def test_busy_retiree_does_not_post_the_drain_barrier(self):
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=True), RecordingDriver(idle=False)
+        run(sm, driver, 5)
+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.DRAIN)
+        self.assertNotIn("post_drain_barrier", driver.calls)
+        self.assertFalse(sm.is_terminal())
+
+    def test_busy_survivor_still_posts_the_drain_barrier(self):
+        # Only a retiree's own queue strands work; a survivor keeps serving.
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=False), RecordingDriver(idle=False)
+        run(sm, driver)
+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.COMPLETE)
+
+    def test_retiree_rechecks_idle_before_announcing_departure(self):
+        """Work admitted while the barrier was in flight must hold the departure."""
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=True), RecordingDriver()
+        run(sm, driver, 2)  # PREPARE -> DRAIN, then posts the barrier while idle
+        self.assertIn("post_drain_barrier", driver.calls)
+        driver.idle = False  # a request lands while the rank waits on the barrier
+        run(sm, driver, 2)  # the barrier completes
+        self.assertNotIn("announce_departure", driver.calls)
+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.DRAIN)
+        driver.idle = True
+        run(sm, driver)
+        self.assertIn("announce_departure", driver.calls)
+        self.assertEqual(sm.state, ScaleDownState.EXIT)
+
+    def test_drain_barrier_is_posted_once_per_cycle(self):
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=False), RecordingDriver(barrier_ready=False)
+        run(sm, driver, 6)
+        # Re-posting would double-count arrivals and let a subset pass.
+        self.assertEqual(driver.calls.count("post_drain_barrier"), 1)
+
+    def test_barrier_that_never_arms_fails_instead_of_flipping(self):
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=False), RecordingDriver(barrier_ready=False)
+        sm.BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2
+        sm.tick(driver)  # PREPARE -> DRAIN
+        for _ in range(5):  # force a re-post each tick to exhaust the attempts
+            sm._drain_barrier_handle = None
+            sm.tick(driver)
+        self.assertTrue(sm.is_failed())
+        self.assertIn("failed to arm", sm.last_error)
+        self.assertNotIn("on_flip_mask", driver.calls)
+
+    def test_abandon_releases_a_held_barrier(self):
+        """A leaked barrier leader wedges every later scale. Idempotent."""
+        sm, driver = make_sm(is_retiree=False), RecordingDriver(barrier_ready=False)
+        make_sm(is_retiree=False).abandon(driver)  # nothing held: no release
+        self.assertEqual(driver.consumed, [])
+        run(sm, driver, 2)
+        held = sm._drain_barrier_handle
+        self.assertIsNotNone(held)
+        sm.abandon(driver)
+        sm.abandon(driver)
+        self.assertEqual(driver.consumed, [held])
+        self.assertIsNone(sm._drain_barrier_handle)

+    def test_abandon_survives_a_failing_consume(self):

+    def test_driver_exception_is_captured_as_failure(self):

+

+"""Elastic EP TCPStore barriers, against a real in-process TCPStore: leader election,
+epoch reuse and round keying are about how counters behave under concurrent add."""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=20, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+import threading
+import unittest
+from datetime import timedelta
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+import sglang.srt.elastic_ep.elastic_ep as eep
+from sglang.srt.elastic_ep.elastic_ep import (
+    _BARRIER_NS,
+    _StoreBarrier,
+    cohort_vote_via_store,
+    share_expert_map_via_store,
+)
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+
+class StoreBackedTestCase(CustomTestCase):
+    """Gives each test a fresh TCPStore installed as the process-global one."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        self._store = dist.TCPStore(
+            "127.0.0.1",
+            0,
+            1,
+            True,
+            timeout=timedelta(seconds=30),
+            wait_for_workers=False,
+        )
+        cycles = eep._last_local_cycle_id
+        for patch in (
+            mock.patch.object(eep, "get_global_tcp_store", lambda: self._store),
+            # Barrier epochs are per process; reset so tests do not see each other.
+            mock.patch.dict(cycles, dict.fromkeys(cycles, 0)),
+        ):
+            patch.start()
+            self.addCleanup(patch.stop)
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        del self._store
+        super().tearDown()
+
+
+def _post(store, ns="world", target=1, rank=0):
+    return _StoreBarrier.post(store, rank, ns, target)
+
+
+class TestStoreBarrier(StoreBackedTestCase):
+    def test_first_arrival_is_the_leader_and_peers_follow(self):
+        first = _post(self._store, target=2)
+        self.assertEqual(first.arrival, 1, "first poster should lead")
+        self.assertEqual(first.check(self._store, 0.0), (False, 1), "below its target")
+        # Both ranks share this process's cycle marker, which the leader just advanced;
+        # a real follower has not seen the new id yet, so rewind to stand in for one.
+        eep._last_local_cycle_id["world"] = first.epoch - 1
+        second = _post(self._store, target=2, rank=1)
+        self.assertIsNotNone(second, "follower should adopt the leader's epoch")
+        self.assertNotEqual(second.arrival, 1)
+        # Both must agree on the epoch, or they wait on different ready keys.
+        self.assertEqual(first.epoch, second.epoch)

A Mooncake fault-tolerance deployment without `--max-ep-size` still gets its shrink accepted here, including with Mooncake a2a, which the description lists as out of scope. Could this gate on the same predicate?
