+"""Mooncake-native scale-down state machine (per-rank FSM across scheduler ticks).
+
+    Survivor:  PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> RECONFIG -> COMPLETE
+    Retiree:   PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> LOCAL_CLEANUP -> EXIT
+
+Both barriers rendezvous over the global TCPStore and poll across ticks, so a waiting
+rank keeps servicing mlp_sync where a collective deadlocks. That polling is why leaving
+DRAIN needs a second signal, carried by the mlp_sync (elastic_ep.departure_pending()).
+A retiree enters DRAIN only once its queues are empty, so the barrier is the drain.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum, auto
+from typing import Any, List, Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class ScaleDownState(Enum):
+    PREPARE = auto()
+    DRAIN = auto()
+    NIXL_RETIRE = auto()
+    FLIP_MASK = auto()
+    RECONFIG = auto()  # survivor-only
+    COMPLETE = auto()  # survivor terminal
+    LOCAL_CLEANUP = auto()  # retiree-only
+    EXIT = auto()  # retiree terminal
+    FAILED = auto()
+
+
+_TERMINAL = {ScaleDownState.COMPLETE, ScaleDownState.EXIT, ScaleDownState.FAILED}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ScaleDownStateMachine:
+    """Per-rank scale-down driver owned by ModelRunner; torn down at terminal."""
+
+    is_retiree: bool
+    target_size: int
+    effective_size: int
+    ranks_to_retire: List[int]
+    my_global_rank: int
+    state: ScaleDownState = ScaleDownState.PREPARE
+    last_error: Optional[str] = None
+    _drain_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _drain_post_attempts: int = 0
+    _drain_barrier_done: bool = False
+    _nixl_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _nixl_post_attempts: int = 0
+    # Bounded re-arms, then fail rather than flip the mask unsynchronized.
+    BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS: int = 20
+    # Under the barrier's own 300s timeout, so an absent peer is reported there.
+    RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S: float = 120.0
+
+    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state in _TERMINAL
+
+    def is_failed(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state is ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def tick(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        """Advance by one stage per call. Side effects live in driver callbacks."""
+        if self.is_terminal():
+            return
+        try:
+            self._advance(driver)
+            if self.state is ScaleDownState.EXIT:
+                driver.on_exit(self)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+            logger.error(
+                "[Elastic EP][scale-down FSM] rank=%d %s failed in %s",
+                self.my_global_rank,
+                "retiree" if self.is_retiree else "survivor",
+                self.state.name.lower(),
+                exc_info=True,
+            )
+            self.state = ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def _fold_nixl_to_flip(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        """Same-tick NIXL barrier -> FLIP_MASK -> post-flip."""
+        # Post once per cycle: re-posting double-counts arrivals and lets a subset pass.
+        if self._nixl_barrier_handle is None:
+            self._nixl_post_attempts += 1
+            if self._nixl_post_attempts > self.BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"NIXL retire barrier failed to arm after "
+                    f"{self._nixl_post_attempts - 1} attempts"
+                )
+            self._nixl_barrier_handle = driver.post_nixl_retire_barrier(self)
+            # A retiree blocks rather than polls: it clears the drain barrier first,
+            # so re-ticking would post a control-plane collective against peers
+            # already in reconfig. It has no work left to lose.
+        if not driver.check_barrier(
+            self._nixl_barrier_handle,
+            block_s=self.RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S if self.is_retiree else None,
+        ):
+            return
+        driver.consume_barrier(self._nixl_barrier_handle)
+        if self.is_retiree:
+            driver.on_retiree_quiesce(self)
+        else:
+            driver.on_nixl_retire_pre(self)
+        self._nixl_barrier_handle = None
+        self.state = ScaleDownState.FLIP_MASK
+        driver.on_flip_mask(self)
+        self.state = (
+            ScaleDownState.LOCAL_CLEANUP if self.is_retiree else ScaleDownState.RECONFIG
+        )
+
+    def _advance(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        S = ScaleDownState
+        if self.state is S.PREPARE:
+            driver.on_prepare(self)
+            self.state = S.DRAIN
+            return
+
+        if self.state is S.DRAIN:
+            # Past the barrier, awaiting cohort agreement; serving keeps mlp_sync alive.
+            if self._drain_barrier_done:
+                if not driver.departure_cleared(self):
+                    return
+                self.state = S.NIXL_RETIRE
+                # Gate the batch step here, not at FLIP_MASK: all ranks crossed this
+                # tick, so no serving-loop collective remains, only store barriers.
+                driver.on_depart_drain(self)
+                self._fold_nixl_to_flip(driver)
+                return
+            # Post once per cycle, for the same reason the NIXL barrier does.
+            if self._drain_barrier_handle is None:
+                # A retiree exiting with work in flight strands it: its terminal is
+                # sys.exit(). Ahead of the counter, so decodes burn no attempts.
+                if self.is_retiree and not driver.local_idle(self):
+                    return

This reconcile trusts the mask whenever `mask_dirty` is set. That flag is also set on grow (`activate_ranks`), not only on shrink.

**Shrink.** The reconcile can run before `_apply_dp_size`, `on_scale` and the map truncation. For example, `await_retirees_departed` raises after its 60 s budget, once the survivors are already past `try_retire_ranks`.
- `effective_ep_size` moves to the target, while dp_size, the expert map and the DPC slots stay at the old width.
- After any earlier scale-up, the next mlp_sync then raises "dp_size is out of sync".

**Grow.** On a failed grow, the tokenizer widens its control fan-out onto slots the DPC never activated.

Could the reconcile be limited to shrinks that got past `_apply_dp_size`, or could the failure path roll dp_size and the map back along with it?

This changes the offset-0 fault-recovery path.
- On base, `try_recover_ranks` / `join_process_groups` ran `recover_ranks` / `join_group`, with the peer-state wait, on every live GroupCoordinator's PGs.

One rank failing mid-way through `reshuffle_for_scale` can hang its peers.
- The failing rank skips its remaining chunks but still attends each `dist.barrier()`.
- Its peers' chunk plans still post isend/irecv to it, so they block in the p2p wait before they ever reach the barrier.
- If it fails in the last chunk instead, this `except` downgrades the "layout may diverge" error to a warning, and the rank keeps serving a layout that differs from its peers'.

This runs by default (`SGLANG_ELASTIC_SYNC_REBALANCE=True`). Could each chunk's outcome be voted before the p2p ops are posted, with a divergent layout treated as fatal, like the orphan-reload path?

When this timeout branch drops `_scale_down_sm`, it doesn't release the FSM's in-flight barrier handle.

Only the leader resets ARRIVAL (`_StoreBarrier.consume`), so if this rank led the round, the counter stays high. That happens when a retiree's drain outlasts the 300 s barrier timeout but not the 600 s scale timeout.
- The next shrink has no leader.
- Its followers adopt the orphaned epoch with its stale count, and the cohort crosses one rank short.
- No later round ever gets a leader again.

Could this path consume both handles, e.g. through a `release()` on the FSM?

inline_comments.body:
In `external` mode this park runs with the scheduler's hard watchdog still armed.
- If the last iteration ran a batch, `cur_batch_for_debug` is still set; it is reassigned only after `get_next_batch_to_run`.
- Nothing advances `forward_ct` from here, so after `--watchdog-timeout` the retiree SIGQUITs its parent.
- On a single-node shrink, that parent is the primary's launcher, which takes the survivors down with it unless the orchestrator has already terminated the retiree.

Could the scheduler own this terminal state, so it can disarm the watchdog before parking?

inline_comments.body:
`seed_barrier_epochs()` runs after this joiner has already posted `scale_ready`. In that namespace it therefore has exactly the "no floor" problem the seed docstring describes.

If the joiner arrives as a follower between the leader's arrival add and its cycle add, it adopts the previous epoch, and it crosses alone because that epoch's ready key already holds the full count.

Seeding next to `clear_expert_map_inbox`, before the announce, closes the window: no survivor can start this grow's ready round until the joiner has registered.

inline_comments.body:
`model_runner.py` is a frozen file: orchestration only, per `.claude/skills/large-class-style/SKILL.md`. This PR adds about +650/−160 lines to it, most of them domain logic:
- orphan repair (`_repair_orphan_logicals`)
- relabel diffing (`_local_relabelled_logicals`)
- metadata truncation (`_shrink_eplb_metadata_for_scale`)
- the seed-over-store protocol (`_sync_random_seed_via_store`)
- `maybe_retire_ep_ranks`, `_finalize_scale_down` and `_retire_and_exit`
- this whole `_ScaleDownDriver` class

Could the scale-down side live in an elastic-EP collaborator next to `scale_down_state.py`, taking narrow args, with `ModelRunner` delegating once per tick? That would also make the FSM driver unit-testable without a runner.

+            orphans = [l for l in range(num_logical) if counts[l] == 0]
+            if not orphans:
+                continue
+            repaired[layer_id] = list(orphans)
+            for orphan in orphans:
+                for slot_idx, value in enumerate(row):
+                    if 0 <= value < num_logical and counts[value] >= 2:
+                        counts[value] -= 1
+                        row[slot_idx] = orphan
+                        counts[orphan] = 1
+                        break
+                else:
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        f"Layer {layer_id}: no duplicate to cover logical {orphan}; "
+                        "increase --ep-num-redundant-experts."
+                    )
+            shrunk_p2l[layer_id] = torch.tensor(
+                row, dtype=shrunk_p2l.dtype, device=shrunk_p2l.device
+            )
+
+        if repaired:
+            logger.warning(
+                "[Elastic EP] shrink orphaned %d logical expert(s) across %d layer(s); "
+                "reloading their weights (the donor slots hold the wrong ones): %s",
+                sum(len(v) for v in repaired.values()),
+                len(repaired),
+                {k: v for k, v in list(repaired.items())[:4]},
+            )
+        return repaired
+
+    def _reload_relabelled_expert_weights(
+        self, per_layer: dict[int, list[int]]
+    ) -> None:
+        """Fetch weights for logicals whose slot does not hold them yet."""
+        from sglang.srt.eplb.eplb_manager import reload_missing_expert_weights
+
+        if not per_layer:
+            return
+        reload_missing_expert_weights(
+            per_layer,
+            model=self.model,
+            expert_backup_client=self.expert_backup_client,
+            update_weights_from_disk_callable=self.weight_updater.update_weights_from_disk,
+        )
+
+    def _finalize_scale_down(
+        self,
+        ranks_to_retire: list[int],
+        target_size: int,
+        effective_size: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Survivor tail: MoE / dp_attn / expert-location rebuild + commit. No PG rebuild."""
+        from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import ElasticScaleUpdateReq
+
+        await_retirees_departed(ranks_to_retire)
+        ElasticEPStateManager.mark_phase("reconfiguring")
+        self.forward_pass_id = 0
+
+        if self.eplb_manager is not None:
+            self.eplb_manager.reset_generator()
+
+        # No broadcast: every survivor repairs the same pre-shrink map by the same rule,
+        # so it already holds what one would send. Grow needs one; a joiner has no map.
+        self._shrink_eplb_metadata_for_scale(
+            from_ep_size=effective_size,
+            effective_size=target_size,
+        )
+
+        ElasticEPStateManager.on_scale(effective_size, target_size)
+
+        if self.eplb_manager is not None:
+            self.eplb_manager.disable_rebalance("EPLB disabled during scale-down")
+
+        self._apply_dp_size(target_size, self._elastic_global_rank())
+
+        ElasticEPStateManager.mark_syncing_new_world()
+        # Drain lingering GPU work still holding an RDMA slot to a retiree pre-barrier.
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        # Commit before the barrier, so a stuck Mooncake cannot strand pre-shrink ep_size
+        # against a post-shrink dp/mask.
+        ElasticEPStateManager.commit_scale()
+        self._elastic_scale_ready_barrier(target_size=target_size, log_tag="SURVIVOR")
+        # Shrink only: on grow the rejoining rank would take experts before Mooncake
+        # settled its links, and the p2p wait hangs uninterruptibly.
+        if self.eplb_manager is not None and envs.SGLANG_ELASTIC_SYNC_REBALANCE.get():
+            try:
+                self.eplb_manager.reshuffle_for_scale(target_size)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                # The repaired mapping stands and EPLB retries.
+                logger.warning("[Elastic EP] scale reshuffle failed: %s", exc)
+        self._reinit_expert_distribution_recorder(self._elastic_global_rank())
+        self._rearm_eplb_after_elastic_scale()
+
+        if self._elastic_global_rank() == 0:
+            self._pending_elastic_scale_update = ElasticScaleUpdateReq(
+                success=True,
+                effective_ep_size=target_size,
+                slot_offset=target_size,
+                slot_count=effective_size - target_size,
+                direction="shrink",
+            )
+
+
+class _ScaleDownDriver:
+    """FSM driver: bridges state transitions to ModelRunner side effects."""

This block runs for every Mooncake elastic launch, not just ones that can scale:
- **It writes a process env var from a resolution hook.** Other hooks declare values instead of writing global state. The default is True, so the warning always fires, and in `Engine` mode the change leaks into the caller's process.
- **The new rejections apply to all of them.** `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` and `--enable-symm-mem` are now refused for fault-tolerance-only users too.
- **So does the Mooncake version floor.** `ElasticEPStateManager.init` now requires `mooncake.pg.deactivate_ranks`, so those users can no longer boot on Mooncake older than 0.3.13.

Could all of this be gated on `scaling_active`? And could the broadcaster choice reach group construction as a resolved value instead of through `os.environ`?

- The pure-Python parts have no unit tests: the `ScaleDownStateMachine` transitions, `elastic_stage_plan`, `_repair_orphan_logicals`, and the `_StoreBarrier` epoch election against a fake store.

Took the second option. `query_mask_buffer` now runs on a stride,
plus once whenever the width pair changes, and is skipped only while a shrink is pending.

Polling on connected set drift cannot be restored, because `get_nixl_buffer` reconciles
`connected_ep_size` to the new width before the combine runs. Drift is therefore already false
by the time the dispatch looks, so a peer that dies at a steady width is still never surfaced.
The cadence is what actually detects it.

The stride exposed a further bug, MC04 and MC10: it read stale transport marks across a width
change, since the transport never clears the mark for a rank it disconnected and a regrow
reconnects without resetting it. Fixed by rebasing on the marks standing at the current width
and treating only a bit that sets afterwards as a fault. MC10 went 0/4 to 3/3 and the benchmark
lanes stayed green.

+"""Mooncake-native scale-down state machine (per-rank FSM across scheduler ticks).
+
+    Survivor:  PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> RECONFIG -> COMPLETE
+    Retiree:   PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> LOCAL_CLEANUP -> EXIT
+
+Both barriers rendezvous over the global TCPStore and poll across ticks, so a waiting
+rank keeps servicing mlp_sync where a collective deadlocks. That polling is why leaving
+DRAIN needs a second signal, carried by the mlp_sync (elastic_ep.departure_pending()).
+A retiree enters DRAIN only once its queues are empty, so the barrier is the drain.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum, auto
+from typing import Any, List, Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class ScaleDownState(Enum):
+    PREPARE = auto()
+    DRAIN = auto()
+    NIXL_RETIRE = auto()
+    FLIP_MASK = auto()
+    RECONFIG = auto()  # survivor-only
+    COMPLETE = auto()  # survivor terminal
+    LOCAL_CLEANUP = auto()  # retiree-only
+    EXIT = auto()  # retiree terminal
+    FAILED = auto()
+
+
+_TERMINAL = {ScaleDownState.COMPLETE, ScaleDownState.EXIT, ScaleDownState.FAILED}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ScaleDownStateMachine:
+    """Per-rank scale-down driver owned by ModelRunner; torn down at terminal."""
+
+    is_retiree: bool
+    target_size: int
+    effective_size: int
+    ranks_to_retire: List[int]
+    my_global_rank: int
+    state: ScaleDownState = ScaleDownState.PREPARE
+    last_error: Optional[str] = None
+    _drain_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _drain_post_attempts: int = 0
+    _drain_barrier_done: bool = False
+    _nixl_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _nixl_post_attempts: int = 0
+    # Bounded re-arms, then fail rather than flip the mask unsynchronized.
+    BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS: int = 20
+    # Under the barrier's own 300s timeout, so an absent peer is reported there.
+    RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S: float = 120.0
+
+    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state in _TERMINAL
+
+    def is_failed(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state is ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def tick(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        """Advance by one stage per call. Side effects live in driver callbacks."""
+        if self.is_terminal():
+            return
+        try:
+            self._advance(driver)
+            if self.state is ScaleDownState.EXIT:
+                driver.on_exit(self)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+            logger.error(
+                "[Elastic EP][scale-down FSM] rank=%d %s failed in %s",
+                self.my_global_rank,
+                "retiree" if self.is_retiree else "survivor",
+                self.state.name.lower(),
+                exc_info=True,
+            )
+            self.state = ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def _fold_nixl_to_flip(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        """Same-tick NIXL barrier -> FLIP_MASK -> post-flip."""
+        # Post once per cycle: re-posting double-counts arrivals and lets a subset pass.
+        if self._nixl_barrier_handle is None:
+            self._nixl_post_attempts += 1
+            if self._nixl_post_attempts > self.BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"NIXL retire barrier failed to arm after "
+                    f"{self._nixl_post_attempts - 1} attempts"
+                )
+            self._nixl_barrier_handle = driver.post_nixl_retire_barrier(self)
+            # A retiree blocks rather than polls: it clears the drain barrier first,
+            # so re-ticking would post a control-plane collective against peers
+            # already in reconfig. It has no work left to lose.
+        if not driver.check_barrier(
+            self._nixl_barrier_handle,
+            block_s=self.RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S if self.is_retiree else None,
+        ):
+            return
+        driver.consume_barrier(self._nixl_barrier_handle)
+        if self.is_retiree:
+            driver.on_retiree_quiesce(self)
+        else:
+            driver.on_nixl_retire_pre(self)
+        self._nixl_barrier_handle = None
+        self.state = ScaleDownState.FLIP_MASK
+        driver.on_flip_mask(self)
+        self.state = (
+            ScaleDownState.LOCAL_CLEANUP if self.is_retiree else ScaleDownState.RECONFIG
+        )
+
+    def _advance(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        S = ScaleDownState
+        if self.state is S.PREPARE:
+            driver.on_prepare(self)
+            self.state = S.DRAIN
+            return
+
+        if self.state is S.DRAIN:
+            # Past the barrier, awaiting cohort agreement; serving keeps mlp_sync alive.
+            if self._drain_barrier_done:
+                if not driver.departure_cleared(self):
+                    return
+                self.state = S.NIXL_RETIRE
+                # Gate the batch step here, not at FLIP_MASK: all ranks crossed this
+                # tick, so no serving-loop collective remains, only store barriers.
+                driver.on_depart_drain(self)
+                self._fold_nixl_to_flip(driver)
+                return
+            # Post once per cycle, for the same reason the NIXL barrier does.
+            if self._drain_barrier_handle is None:
+                # A retiree exiting with work in flight strands it: its terminal is
+                # sys.exit(). Ahead of the counter, so decodes burn no attempts.
+                if self.is_retiree and not driver.local_idle(self):
+                    return

Both implemented. I thought the cohort votes around the loop already covered this, but they did not. The vote ran once after all chunks, so your hang was still reachable.

The outcome is now voted per chunk, which stops the cohort before the next chunk's p2p ops go
out. The verdict is also split, so fatal means fatal. An abort with nothing installed returns
`False` and stays retryable. Stopping after a chunk landed raises a new
`ExpertLayoutDivergence`, which the finalizer no longer downgrades to a warning. It propagates
like the orphan reload you cite.

+            return
+
+        # is_shrink_pending() already implies a live instance and pending < effective.
+        inst = ElasticEPStateManager.instance()
+        pending_size = ElasticEPStateManager.get_pending_ep_size()
+        effective_size = ElasticEPStateManager.get_effective_ep_size()
+        if (
+            time.monotonic() - inst.pending_since
+            > self.server_args.elastic_ep_scale_timeout
+        ):
+            error = f"Timed out waiting for cohort at retire barrier (target={pending_size})"
+            self._fail_scale(error, effective_size)
+            self._scale_down_sm = None
+            return
+
+        # Lazy: construct on first pending-shrink tick, tear down on terminal.
+        sm = getattr(self, "_scale_down_sm", None)
+        if sm is None:
+            ranks_to_retire = list(range(pending_size, effective_size))
+            my_global_rank = self._elastic_global_rank()
+            sm = ScaleDownStateMachine(
+                is_retiree=my_global_rank in ranks_to_retire,
+                target_size=pending_size,
+                effective_size=effective_size,
+                ranks_to_retire=ranks_to_retire,
+                my_global_rank=my_global_rank,
+            )
+            self._scale_down_sm = sm
+
+        sm.tick(_ScaleDownDriver(self, getattr(self, "_elastic_is_idle", None)))
+        if sm.is_failed():
+            self._fail_scale(
+                sm.last_error or "unknown scale-down FSM failure", effective_size
+            )
+        # FAILED is terminal, so this also tears down after the failure above.
+        if sm.is_terminal():
+            self._scale_down_sm = None
+
+    def _retire_and_exit(self) -> None:
+        """Retiree terminal: exit, or park for an orchestrator. FSM EXIT after cleanup."""
+        my_rank = self._elastic_global_rank()
+        if get_exec().moe.elastic_ep_retiree_lifecycle == "external":
+            # Never return: the caller's event loop would collect on destroyed groups.
+            logger.info(
+                "[Elastic EP][retire] rank=%d parked; awaiting external termination",
+                my_rank,
+            )
+            while True:
+                time.sleep(5.0)
+        sys.exit(0)
+
+    def _shrink_eplb_metadata_for_scale(
+        self, from_ep_size: int, effective_size: int
+    ) -> None:
+        """Truncate physical_to_logical_map to survivor slots + repair orphaned logicals."""
+        metadata = get_global_expert_location_metadata()
+        if metadata is None:
+            return
+        old_num_physical = metadata.num_physical_experts
+        num_local = old_num_physical // from_ep_size
+        new_num_physical = num_local * effective_size
+        if new_num_physical >= old_num_physical:
+            return
+
+        get_context().override("elastic_ep.scale", ep_size=effective_size)
+        # clone(), not contiguous(): a single-MoE-layer slice is already contiguous, so
+        # the repair below would write through into the still-installed metadata.
+        shrunk_p2l = metadata.physical_to_logical_map[:, :new_num_physical].clone()
+        relabelled = self._repair_orphan_logicals(
+            shrunk_p2l=shrunk_p2l, num_logical=metadata.num_logical_experts
+        )
+        new_metadata = ExpertLocationMetadata.init_by_mapping(
+            self.model_config,
+            physical_to_logical_map=shrunk_p2l,
+            moe_ep_rank=self._elastic_global_rank(),
+        )
+        metadata.adopt_scaled_in_place(new_metadata)
+        # After the map is installed, so the loader follows it. Fatal on failure: the map
+        # claims a slot holds the orphan while it still holds its donor.
+        try:
+            self._reload_relabelled_expert_weights(relabelled)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Elastic EP shrink left this rank's expert weights out of sync with "
+                f"its expert map ({exc}). It must not continue serving."
+            ) from exc
+
+    def _repair_orphan_logicals(
+        self, *, shrunk_p2l: torch.Tensor, num_logical: int
+    ) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
+        """Ensure every logical has >= 1 physical replica by reassigning duplicated slots.
+
+        Returns the logicals relabelled onto a donor slot. Relabelling moves the mapping
+        only and the p2p diffs labels, so the caller must reload these from backup."""
+        num_layers, new_num_physical = shrunk_p2l.shape
+        if new_num_physical < num_logical:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Shrink leaves {new_num_physical} slots for {num_logical} logicals; "
+                "increase --ep-num-redundant-experts."
+            )
+
+        # Keyed by the global layer id the weight-name filter parses.
+        repaired: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
+        for layer_id in range(num_layers):
+            row = shrunk_p2l[layer_id].tolist()
+            counts = [0] * num_logical
+            for value in row:
+                if 0 <= value < num_logical:
+                    counts[value] += 1
+            orphans = [l for l in range(num_logical) if counts[l] == 0]
+            if not orphans:
+                continue
+            repaired[layer_id] = list(orphans)
+            for orphan in orphans:
+                for slot_idx, value in enumerate(row):
+                    if 0 <= value < num_logical and counts[value] >= 2:
+                        counts[value] -= 1
+                        row[slot_idx] = orphan
+                        counts[orphan] = 1
+                        break
+                else:
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        f"Layer {layer_id}: no duplicate to cover logical {orphan}; "
+                        "increase --ep-num-redundant-experts."
+                    )
+            shrunk_p2l[layer_id] = torch.tensor(
+                row, dtype=shrunk_p2l.dtype, device=shrunk_p2l.device
+            )
+
+        if repaired:
+            logger.warning(
+                "[Elastic EP] shrink orphaned %d logical expert(s) across %d layer(s); "
+                "reloading their weights (the donor slots hold the wrong ones): %s",
+                sum(len(v) for v in repaired.values()),
+                len(repaired),
+                {k: v for k, v in list(repaired.items())[:4]},
+            )
+        return repaired
+
+    def _reload_relabelled_expert_weights(
+        self, per_layer: dict[int, list[int]]
+    ) -> None:
+        """Fetch weights for logicals whose slot does not hold them yet."""
+        from sglang.srt.eplb.eplb_manager import reload_missing_expert_weights
+
+        if not per_layer:
+            return
+        reload_missing_expert_weights(
+            per_layer,
+            model=self.model,
+            expert_backup_client=self.expert_backup_client,
+            update_weights_from_disk_callable=self.weight_updater.update_weights_from_disk,
+        )
+
+    def _finalize_scale_down(
+        self,
+        ranks_to_retire: list[int],
+        target_size: int,
+        effective_size: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Survivor tail: MoE / dp_attn / expert-location rebuild + commit. No PG rebuild."""
+        from sglang.srt.managers.io_struct import ElasticScaleUpdateReq
+
+        await_retirees_departed(ranks_to_retire)
+        ElasticEPStateManager.mark_phase("reconfiguring")
+        self.forward_pass_id = 0
+
+        if self.eplb_manager is not None:
+            self.eplb_manager.reset_generator()
+
+        # No broadcast: every survivor repairs the same pre-shrink map by the same rule,
+        # so it already holds what one would send. Grow needs one; a joiner has no map.
+        self._shrink_eplb_metadata_for_scale(
+            from_ep_size=effective_size,
+            effective_size=target_size,
+        )
+
+        ElasticEPStateManager.on_scale(effective_size, target_size)
+
+        if self.eplb_manager is not None:
+            self.eplb_manager.disable_rebalance("EPLB disabled during scale-down")
+
+        self._apply_dp_size(target_size, self._elastic_global_rank())
+
+        ElasticEPStateManager.mark_syncing_new_world()
+        # Drain lingering GPU work still holding an RDMA slot to a retiree pre-barrier.
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        # Commit before the barrier, so a stuck Mooncake cannot strand pre-shrink ep_size
+        # against a post-shrink dp/mask.
+        ElasticEPStateManager.commit_scale()
+        self._elastic_scale_ready_barrier(target_size=target_size, log_tag="SURVIVOR")
+        # Shrink only: on grow the rejoining rank would take experts before Mooncake
+        # settled its links, and the p2p wait hangs uninterruptibly.
+        if self.eplb_manager is not None and envs.SGLANG_ELASTIC_SYNC_REBALANCE.get():
+            try:
+                self.eplb_manager.reshuffle_for_scale(target_size)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                # The repaired mapping stands and EPLB retries.
+                logger.warning("[Elastic EP] scale reshuffle failed: %s", exc)
+        self._reinit_expert_distribution_recorder(self._elastic_global_rank())
+        self._rearm_eplb_after_elastic_scale()
+
+        if self._elastic_global_rank() == 0:
+            self._pending_elastic_scale_update = ElasticScaleUpdateReq(
+                success=True,
+                effective_ep_size=target_size,
+                slot_offset=target_size,
+                slot_count=effective_size - target_size,
+                direction="shrink",
+            )
+
+
+class _ScaleDownDriver:
+    """FSM driver: bridges state transitions to ModelRunner side effects."""

+    def _post(self, path: str, timeout: float = 60, **kw) -> requests.Response:

+            "error",
+            result,
+            f"decode on the retired rank did not survive the shrink: "
+            f"{result.get('error')}",

+        meta = result["body"].get("meta_info", {})
+        self.assertEqual(
+            meta.get("completion_tokens"),
+            self.DECODE_TOKENS,
+            f"decode on the retired rank was truncated; ignore_eos was set so the "
+            f"length should be exact: meta={meta}",
+        )
+

On the BF16 flag, one correction first, because the rest follows from it. Mooncake a2a is not
out of scope here. It is the subject: the PR is Mooncake native scale down, and shrink over
Mooncake is supported and certified. `MC02C` shrinks 4 to 3 on one node, `MC05M` retires a
whole worker node 8 to 4 across the fabric, and `RECOVER` gets ranks back after a bare fault,
all over Mooncake a2a. If the description implied otherwise it was unclear, and it now states
the boundary outright.

What is out of scope over Mooncake is scale **up**, and that limit is already upstream's rather
than something this PR chose. `parallel_hook.py` asserts
`resolved.moe_a2a_backend == "nixl"` for scale up, and it fires whenever
`max_ep_size > tp_size`. So a Mooncake deployment runs with `max_ep_size` at the launch width.
A shrink needs no headroom above that width and is unaffected. A regrow does need it, because a
retired slot is repopulated by a joiner and the joiner requires the same setting. Mooncake
therefore gets `8 -> 4` but not `4 -> 3 -> 4`. Every regrow and append lane in the sweep runs
NIXL for exactly that reason.

**(1) Fixed, both halves.** You were right, and the reason the tokenizer half looked
impossible was a bug on our side rather than a property of the design. Thank you for holding
the line on it.

The DPC half is in. `_dispatch_elastic_scale_request` forwards the scale request and then stops
routing new work to the retiring slots, and `_redirect_if_draining` moves the budget and
bootstrap room pickers off them too. Retirees still receive control messages, since they need
the scale request itself to start draining. `_dispatch_elastic_scale_update` clears the set on
commit and on failure.

The tokenizer half is now in too. The gate holds a request only if it carries an explicit
`routed_dp_rank` onto a slot that is leaving. Everything else is admitted for the whole shrink.

What blocked it was one term in the retiree's idle test. Under dp attention a rank with no
tokens of its own still builds `get_idle_batch()` and runs a forward whenever any survivor
holds tokens, `dp_attn.py:578`. `ScheduleBatch` defines neither `__bool__` nor `__len__`, so
that empty batch is truthy at `scheduler.py:2000`, the forward runs, and the result lands in
`result_queue`. `is_fully_idle` refuses while that queue is not empty under overlap, and
`tick_elastic_scale` runs at the top of the loop, before that iteration's pop, so the retiree's
tick always saw a queue of one. A fully drained retiree therefore never reported idle and never
posted the drain barrier. That is the 3/4 barrier expiry we had measured, and we had read it as
the cohort disagreeing on a collective sequence. It was not.

requests of its own, not that no forward is in flight. An idle batch carries no request, so a
pending idle batch result strands nothing on exit. `is_fully_idle` takes an

|---|---|---|
| admission blackout, eager | 24.7 s | **0.9 s** |

| worst in flight stall, eager | 71 ms | 138 ms |
| admission blackout, decode graphs on | 11.2 s | **9.1 s** |

tail, but it is not free. And the graphs on arm improves much less because its blackout is
dominated by the decode graph recapture rather than by the gate, so scoping the gate can only
take out the part the gate owned.

holds under sustained load rather than only when the in flight requests are short, and the
description carries the measured numbers.

schedulers refuse, on both the rejection path and the exception path. An orchestrator polling

+"""Mooncake-native scale-down state machine (per-rank FSM across scheduler ticks).
+
+    Survivor:  PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> RECONFIG -> COMPLETE
+    Retiree:   PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> LOCAL_CLEANUP -> EXIT
+
+Both barriers rendezvous over the global TCPStore and poll across ticks, so a waiting
+rank keeps servicing mlp_sync where a collective deadlocks. That polling is why leaving
+DRAIN needs a second signal, carried by the mlp_sync (elastic_ep.departure_pending()).
+A retiree enters DRAIN only once its queues are empty, so the barrier is the drain.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum, auto
+from typing import Any, List, Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class ScaleDownState(Enum):
+    PREPARE = auto()
+    DRAIN = auto()
+    NIXL_RETIRE = auto()
+    FLIP_MASK = auto()
+    RECONFIG = auto()  # survivor-only
+    COMPLETE = auto()  # survivor terminal
+    LOCAL_CLEANUP = auto()  # retiree-only
+    EXIT = auto()  # retiree terminal
+    FAILED = auto()
+
+
+_TERMINAL = {ScaleDownState.COMPLETE, ScaleDownState.EXIT, ScaleDownState.FAILED}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ScaleDownStateMachine:
+    """Per-rank scale-down driver owned by ModelRunner; torn down at terminal."""
+
+    is_retiree: bool
+    target_size: int
+    effective_size: int
+    ranks_to_retire: List[int]
+    my_global_rank: int
+    state: ScaleDownState = ScaleDownState.PREPARE
+    last_error: Optional[str] = None
+    _drain_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _drain_post_attempts: int = 0
+    _drain_barrier_done: bool = False
+    _departure_announced: bool = False
+    _nixl_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _nixl_post_attempts: int = 0
+    # Bounded re-arms, then fail rather than flip the mask unsynchronized.
+    BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS: int = 20
+    # Under the barrier's own 300s timeout, so an absent peer is reported there.
+    RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S: float = 120.0
+
+    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state in _TERMINAL
+
+    def abandon(self, driver) -> None:
+        """Release any barrier this rank posted, before the machine is discarded.
+
+        The store barriers are leader-based: whoever posted an epoch first owes the
+        ARRIVAL reset. Dropping the machine with a handle outstanding leaves that epoch
+        held, and the next cycle's first arrival then never reads 1, so every later
+        scale waits on a barrier that can no longer arm. Idempotent."""
+        for attr in ("_drain_barrier_handle", "_nixl_barrier_handle"):
+            handle = getattr(self, attr)
+            if handle is None:
+                continue
+            setattr(self, attr, None)
+            try:
+                driver.consume_barrier(handle)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "[Elastic EP] releasing %s during teardown failed",
+                    attr,
+                    exc_info=True,
+                )
+
+    def is_failed(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state is ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def tick(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        """Advance by one stage per call. Side effects live in driver callbacks."""
+        if self.is_terminal():
+            return
+        try:
+            self._advance(driver)
+            if self.state is ScaleDownState.EXIT:
+                driver.on_exit(self)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+            logger.error(

+                self.my_global_rank,

For a joiner with `tp_size > 1` this never returns a width. The joiner writes its announce once, from tp_rank 0, under its own offset (`model_runner.py:537`). This check, however, requires a key for every slot in `recover_slots`.

Example: launch 8, shrink 8→4, start a `tp_size=2` joiner at offset 4, then grow to 6.
- The joiner's width equals the target, which is the case the last commit makes direct, but slot 5 has no key.
- The tokenizer retries for 120 s while holding `_elastic_scale_lock`, then stages through 8.
- Slots 6–7 have no joiner, so the grow fails.

MC17 and MC21 each cover a single recover slot, so neither hits this. Could the joiner announce every slot it covers, or could this look up the announce whose span contains each slot?

+    map. Only safe ahead of the announce, past which the source may have written."""
+    store = _store_or_none("[Elastic EP][expert map]")
+    if store is not None:
+        store.delete_key(_EXPERT_MAP_INBOX_KEY.format(group_rank))
+
+
+def share_expert_map_via_store(
+    tensor: torch.Tensor, *, is_src: bool, cohort_size: int, group_rank: int
+) -> bool:
+    """Hand the expert map to the cohort over the store, one inbox per reader. False = no
+    store, caller falls back to the collective. Not a broadcast: Mooncake drives one through
+    putTaskCuda, which syncs the stream from inside the collective. An inbox, not a shared
+    round, since a round keyed on participant count desyncs when the width changes."""
+    store = _store_or_none("[Elastic EP][expert map]")
+    if store is None or cohort_size <= 1:
+        return False
+    if is_src:
+        blob = tensor.cpu().numpy().tobytes()
+        for peer in range(cohort_size):
+            if peer != group_rank:
+                store.set(_EXPERT_MAP_INBOX_KEY.format(peer), blob)
+        return True
+    key = _EXPERT_MAP_INBOX_KEY.format(group_rank)
+    staged = torch.frombuffer(bytearray(store.get(key)), dtype=tensor.dtype)
+    # Leave it empty so the next round blocks rather than being served this one.
+    store.delete_key(key)
+    tensor.copy_(staged.view(tensor.shape))
+    return True
+
+
+def sync_random_seed_via_store(is_source: bool) -> None:
+    """Broadcast random_seed via TCPStore, not broadcast_pyobj: retirees may have left
+    WORLD. Readers wait() rather than poll check() (libuv stalls it 30s) and seed the
+    RNGs directly, since server_args is read-only."""
+    import datetime
+
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_device
+    from sglang.srt.utils import set_random_seed
+
+    key = "sglang_elastic_ep_random_seed"
+    store = _store_or_none("[Elastic EP] random_seed sync:")
+    if store is None:
+        return
+
+    if is_source:
+        try:
+            # get_device(), not server_args: the raw field is None until the device
+            # namespace resolves it, so int() raised and no key was ever written.
+            store.set(key, str(int(get_device().random_seed)))
+        except Exception as exc:
+            logger.warning("[Elastic EP] random_seed source write failed (%s)", exc)
+        return
+
+    try:
+        store.wait([key], datetime.timedelta(seconds=30))
+        set_random_seed(_store_int(store, key))
+    except Exception as exc:
+        logger.warning(
+            "[Elastic EP] random_seed sync failed (%s); keeping boot-time value",
+            exc,
+        )
+
+
+def _assert_shrink_runtime_supported() -> None:
+    """The invariants the FSM itself needs, re-checked at shrink-request time.
+
+    A no-op for a deployment that opted into scaling: parallel_hook asserts each of
+    these at launch, but only when ``--max-ep-size > tp_size``. The point is the
+    fault-tolerance deployment that never sets it, whose shrink would otherwise be
+    accepted while skipping every one of them.
+    """
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_disagg, get_serving
+
+    parallel = get_parallel()
+    disagg = get_disagg()
+    # Only the base event loops tick the FSM; the others drop a scale silently.
+    for ok, requirement in (
+        (
+            parallel.pp_size == 1,
+            f"--pp-size 1 (got {parallel.pp_size}); WORLD must not span PP stages",
+        ),
+        (not disagg.enable_pdmux, "--enable-pdmux to be off"),
+        (
+            disagg.disaggregation_mode == "null",
+            f"no disaggregation (got {disagg.disaggregation_mode})",
+        ),
+        (
+            get_serving().tokenizer_worker_num == 1,
+            f"--tokenizer-worker-num 1 (got {get_serving().tokenizer_worker_num})",
+        ),
+        (
+            parallel.load_balance_method == "round_robin",
+            "--load-balance-method round_robin, so a retired slot stops being "
+            f"handed work (got {parallel.load_balance_method})",
+        ),
+        (
+            # attn_dp_enabled, not enable_dp_attention: the latter is the deprecated
+            # spelling, and parallel_hook consumes it into attn_dp_size and leaves it
+            # False, so reading it rejects every deployment that passed it.
+            parallel.attn_dp_enabled,
+            "--attn-dp-size > 1: the shrink retires EP ranks as DP slots",
+        ),
+    ):
+        if not ok:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Elastic EP scale-down requires {requirement}.")
+
+
+def assert_shrink_supported() -> None:
+    """Fail a shrink request this deployment cannot serve.
+
+    Checked here rather than at init: a fault-tolerance-only deployment never retires a
+    rank, so requiring this at startup would stop an existing one from booting on a
+    mooncake that is perfectly adequate for what it does. A planned shrink without it
+    reads as a link fault (~10s/peer)."""
+    _assert_shrink_runtime_supported()

+"""Mooncake-native scale-down state machine (per-rank FSM across scheduler ticks).
+
+    Survivor:  PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> RECONFIG -> COMPLETE
+    Retiree:   PREPARE -> DRAIN --barrier-- NIXL_RETIRE --barrier-- FLIP_MASK -> LOCAL_CLEANUP -> EXIT
+
+Both barriers rendezvous over the global TCPStore and poll across ticks, so a waiting
+rank keeps servicing mlp_sync where a collective deadlocks. That polling is why leaving
+DRAIN needs a second signal, carried by the mlp_sync (elastic_ep.departure_pending()).
+A retiree enters DRAIN only once its queues are empty, so the barrier is the drain.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum, auto
+from typing import Any, List, Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class ScaleDownState(Enum):
+    PREPARE = auto()
+    DRAIN = auto()
+    NIXL_RETIRE = auto()
+    FLIP_MASK = auto()
+    RECONFIG = auto()  # survivor-only
+    COMPLETE = auto()  # survivor terminal
+    LOCAL_CLEANUP = auto()  # retiree-only
+    EXIT = auto()  # retiree terminal
+    FAILED = auto()
+
+
+_TERMINAL = {ScaleDownState.COMPLETE, ScaleDownState.EXIT, ScaleDownState.FAILED}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ScaleDownStateMachine:
+    """Per-rank scale-down driver owned by ModelRunner; torn down at terminal."""
+
+    is_retiree: bool
+    target_size: int
+    effective_size: int
+    ranks_to_retire: List[int]
+    my_global_rank: int
+    state: ScaleDownState = ScaleDownState.PREPARE
+    last_error: Optional[str] = None
+    _drain_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _drain_post_attempts: int = 0
+    _drain_barrier_done: bool = False
+    _departure_announced: bool = False
+    _nixl_barrier_handle: Optional[object] = None
+    _nixl_post_attempts: int = 0
+    # Bounded re-arms, then fail rather than flip the mask unsynchronized.
+    BARRIER_POST_MAX_ATTEMPTS: int = 20
+    # Under the barrier's own 300s timeout, so an absent peer is reported there.
+    RETIREE_FOLD_BLOCK_S: float = 120.0
+
+    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state in _TERMINAL
+
+    def abandon(self, driver) -> None:
+        """Release any barrier this rank posted, before the machine is discarded.
+
+        The store barriers are leader-based: whoever posted an epoch first owes the
+        ARRIVAL reset. Dropping the machine with a handle outstanding leaves that epoch
+        held, and the next cycle's first arrival then never reads 1, so every later
+        scale waits on a barrier that can no longer arm. Idempotent."""
+        for attr in ("_drain_barrier_handle", "_nixl_barrier_handle"):
+            handle = getattr(self, attr)
+            if handle is None:
+                continue
+            setattr(self, attr, None)
+            try:
+                driver.consume_barrier(handle)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "[Elastic EP] releasing %s during teardown failed",
+                    attr,
+                    exc_info=True,
+                )
+
+    def is_failed(self) -> bool:
+        return self.state is ScaleDownState.FAILED
+
+    def tick(self, driver: Any) -> None:
+        """Advance by one stage per call. Side effects live in driver callbacks."""
+        if self.is_terminal():
+            return
+        try:
+            self._advance(driver)
+            if self.state is ScaleDownState.EXIT:
+                driver.on_exit(self)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            self.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+            logger.error(
+                "[Elastic EP][scale-down FSM] rank=%d %s failed in %s",
+                self.my_global_rank,
+                "retiree" if self.is_retiree else "survivor",
+                self.state.name.lower(),
+                exc_info=True,
+            )
+            self.state = ScaleDownState.FAILED

hides it.

Three guards came with it, because the mask lies in three ways. The transport mask is
both the fault signal and the cause of the outage, and both sides of a stall mark each

Agreed it isn't ideal, but Mooncake gives us nothing stable to match on. Its torch layer raises every failure through a TORCH_CHECK (checkResult in torch/include/torch_utils.h). So this refusal reaches Python as a plain RuntimeError with only a message, and that is still the case on Mooncake main. Reading Mooncake's state after the exception doesn't work either. Mooncake updates its view asynchronously, so the view can change between the refusal and the read.

Within that limit, I had 4cb78d3 kept the match as small as possible. It is one exact constant _MOONCAKE_INACTIVE_REFUSAL (the dp_attn all_gather retry) checked in one place. The settle probe no longer looks at exception text, and mooncake_all_reduce_strict is gone. If Mooncake ever raises a typed error, this becomes a one-line change. I would like to keep it as is for this PR.

inline_comments.body:
Both loops exist because Mooncake PG has no view-convergence signal, so the framework has to wait for convergence itself. A Mooncake-side primitive would be cleaner, but none exists today, and this PR has to work with the Mooncake that ships now.

In 4cb78d3 I cut the sglang side down as far as Mooncake allows:

1. mooncake_world_settle_probe no longer uses a backoff table or trial collectives. It polls Mooncake's own state (get_active_ranks) for up to 15 s, then takes one TCPStore vote.
2. The vote is still needed. Each rank can only read its own view, so the vote keeps every rank out of the next collective until all views have caught up.
3. await_retirees_departed polls get_peer_state, because get_active_ranks only shows our own mask flip, not whether the peer has actually left.

This is the workaround Mooncake's current API allows, and it is confined to these two helpers. I'd like to keep it as is for this PR.

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for pushing scale-down forward. We are looking at this from the Dynamo Kubernetes reconciler in [Dynamo DEP #13121](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13121), and opened [SGLang #35376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35376) for the cross-cutting orchestrator contract.

Two details in this PR are especially important for Kubernetes:

1. **Maximum-capacity cold start.** The pre-shrink design appears to require launching `max_ep_size` physical ranks before retiring to the desired initial size. That means the deployment must obtain its maximum GPU capacity at startup. Could the stable maximum-sized rank mask and buffers be retained while launching only the initial live ranks, then admitting or recovering the remaining slots later? If not, it would be useful to document this as a capability constraint visible to an external orchestrator.

2. **Topology commit versus process exit.** Retirees currently quiesce and call `os._exit(0)` during `flip_mask`, before the survivors finish the full transition to `serving_shrunk`. Depending on the rank-to-container mapping, Kubernetes may restart an exited process/container, and the exit itself does not tell the controller whether the surviving topology committed successfully.

Would it be possible to support an external-process-lifecycle mode where retirees quiesce and wait for termination, while the surviving coordinator reports something like:

```json
{
  "operation_id": "resize-42",
  "phase": "serving_shrunk",
  "effective_ep_size": 4,
  "retired_ranks": [4, 5],
  "safe_to_terminate_ranks": [4, 5]
}
```

That would preserve SGLang's internal drain and commit ordering while letting Kubernetes delete or retain the corresponding capacity safely.

issue_comments.body:
> Thanks for pushing scale-down forward. We are looking at this from the Dynamo Kubernetes reconciler in [Dynamo DEP #13121](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13121), and opened [SGLang #35376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35376) for the cross-cutting orchestrator contract.
> 
> Two details in this PR are especially important for Kubernetes:
> 
> 1. **Maximum-capacity cold start.** The pre-shrink design appears to require launching `max_ep_size` physical ranks before retiring to the desired initial size. That means the deployment must obtain its maximum GPU capacity at startup. Could the stable maximum-sized rank mask and buffers be retained while launching only the initial live ranks, then admitting or recovering the remaining slots later? If not, it would be useful to document this as a capability constraint visible to an external orchestrator.
> 2. **Topology commit versus process exit.** Retirees currently quiesce and call `os._exit(0)` during `flip_mask`, before the survivors finish the full transition to `serving_shrunk`. Depending on the rank-to-container mapping, Kubernetes may restart an exited process/container, and the exit itself does not tell the controller whether the surviving topology committed successfully.
> 
> Would it be possible to support an external-process-lifecycle mode where retirees quiesce and wait for termination, while the surviving coordinator reports something like:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "operation_id": "resize-42",
>   "phase": "serving_shrunk",
>   "effective_ep_size": 4,
>   "retired_ranks": [4, 5],
>   "safe_to_terminate_ranks": [4, 5]
> }
> ```
> 
> That would preserve SGLang's internal drain and commit ordering while letting Kubernetes delete or retain the corresponding capacity safely.

@julienmancuso Thanks, I changed PR based on both points you mentioned. PR description has been updated accordingly

**1. Maximum-capacity cold start.**

`max_ep_size` sizes the rank mask and the backend buffers only. The launched cohort is
independent of it and may be smaller. You can retain the stable maximum-sized
mask and buffers while launching only the initial live ranks, then admit or recover the
remaining slots later, which is exactly the pattern you describe. Three cases in the
sweep launch fewer ranks than the mask width to prove it: MC02B launches 3 into a mask
of 5, MC13 and MC14 launch 4 into a mask of 5.

Pre-shrink is only required for the `recover` join mode, which by definition needs
previously-retired slots to refill. It is one option, not a precondition. The two
patterns are now documented as a table in the PR description.

**2. Topology commit versus process exit.** Added, close to the shape you proposed.

`--elastic-ep-retiree-lifecycle` selects who ends the process:

- `self_exit` (default) — today's behavior, unchanged.
- `external` — the retiree performs the same quiesce, Mooncake deactivation and backend
  teardown, then parks. Your controller terminates it once the survivors have committed.

`/is_scaling_elastic_ep` now reports the commit directly. Full payload:

```json
{
  "is_scaling_elastic_ep": false,
  "effective_ep_size": 4,
  "pending_ep_size": null,
  "scale_phase": "serving_shrunk",
  "last_error": null,
  "operation_id": "resize-42",
  "retired_ranks": [4, 5],
  "safe_to_terminate_ranks": [4, 5]
}

Thanks — the external retiree lifecycle, post-commit `safe_to_terminate_ranks`, smaller-than-maximum cold start, and `warming_up` phase address the main Kubernetes lifecycle concerns we raised.

One remaining contract question: `operation_id` currently appears to be an optional caller tag mirrored in tokenizer-manager status. Could it eventually serve as the idempotency and join-correlation identity for the resize?

Concretely:

- retrying the same `operation_id` and absolute target returns or resumes the existing operation;
- reusing it with a different target is rejected; and
- joining ranks are bound to that operation, or an equivalent topology generation, so a stale joiner from an earlier failed resize cannot be admitted later.

This does not need to expand this PR. Documenting the current boundary and tracking the stronger semantics in RFC #35376 would be sufficient for Dynamo to fail closed meanwhile.

@QiaoK, three capability-boundary questions for replacing a four-rank allocation after one rank has failed:

1. MC08 covers a healthy `8 → 4 → 8`. Can the `8 → 4` shrink run when one rank in the retiring suffix is already inactive? `_barrier_target_from_effective_ep()` sizes the retire barriers to the pre-shrink `effective_ep_size`, while a bare fault does not appear to lower it, so the missing retiree would not arrive and the barrier appears likely to time out. The append-growth admission vote in `maybe_join_ep_ranks` is also sized by `effective_size`, so if growth from a degraded topology is accepted, it appears to encounter the same missing-participant problem; alternatively, it may need to be rejected earlier with an explicit capability error.
2. The known limitations state that an `offset > 0` joiner cannot recover from a bare fault. Is shrink-then-recover intended to become the replacement path for an affected non-primary launch cohort, or is bare-fault recovery at a non-zero offset planned separately?
3. For an affected allocation that is not the high-rank suffix, I assume the current target-size API cannot replace it without selected retirement or remapping. Could you confirm that this remains explicitly out of scope for this PR?

None of these needs to broaden #33111; documenting the supported boundary would be enough for an external orchestrator to choose recovery or group recreation safely.

Thanks @julienmancuso. These are the right three questions, and your read of
`_barrier_target_from_effective_ep()` is correct. A bare fault does not lower
`effective_ep_size`. So a resize admitted on a degraded topology would size its barriers for a
rank that cannot arrive. That is why the resize never gets that far.

**1. An `8 -> 4` with an inactive rank in the retiring suffix is refused at admission, not at a
barrier timeout.**

`is_scaling()` returns true whenever a rank inside the current width is inactive with no scale
pending. `/scale_elastic_ep` rejects on that check above both the shrink and the grow branch.
No barrier is posted, and `_barrier_target_from_effective_ep()` is never reached. This is your
"rejected earlier with an explicit capability error" option.

The same gate sits above the append path. Growth from a degraded topology is refused at the
same point and never reaches the `effective_size` sized vote in `maybe_join_ep_ranks`. Both
directions fail identically.

Your comment did find one real gap. The rejection reused the pending scale message, "a previous
scale operation has not completed yet". That is wrong for a fault, and it would have sent you
looking for an operation that does not exist. It now names the ranks and the reason:

> Ranks [5] are inactive at the current width (8), so no resize can be admitted: its
> barriers would wait on a rank that cannot arrive. Recover those ranks first, or
> recreate the deployment.

`/is_scaling_elastic_ep` reports the same condition. The scheduler logs the inactive set once
when it appears rather than on every poll.

**2. Shrink then recover is not the replacement path. Recovery is.**

Because of (1), a shrink is refused while the fault stands. So shrink then regrow cannot route
around a failed rank. Two paths do exist.

- In place fault recovery, for a cohort that has not yet completed an elastic scale. That is
  `has_scaled` false, which covers a deployment at its launch width with offset 0.
  `maybe_join_ep_ranks` drives `try_recover_ranks` on the inactive set. Once it succeeds the
  width and the mask agree again, `is_scaling()` clears, and an `8 -> 4` is admitted normally.
  This holds on the NIXL all to all backend, which is the one this PR supports for scale down.
  Over Mooncake all to all it is currently broken, and @ch-wan's review thread has the detail.
- Grow into retired slots, for capacity a shrink retired. Slots below the launch width are
  recovered rather than appended. Mixing the two in one request is rejected.

After a committed scale, in place recovery is deliberately not attempted. Failing the state
there would block every future scale. The cohort keeps serving at the reduced mask and reports
the inactive ranks instead, so an orchestrator gets an explanation rather than an opaque
timeout.

Two cases stay out of this PR. Bare fault recovery at a nonzero launch offset, which is separate
work. And bare fault recovery over Mooncake all to all, which raises on the recovered rank's
first expert dispatch. That one is a gap rather than a clean refusal, so if you are driving
Mooncake all to all, treat recovery as unavailable until the follow up lands.

**3. Confirmed out of scope.**

The target size API retires the contiguous high rank suffix only. There is no selected
retirement and no remapping. An affected allocation that is not the suffix cannot be replaced
through this API. That needs group recreation, and I would rather it land with the topology
generation identity from RFC #35376 than be bolted onto absolute target sizes here.

**Documented boundary.** Added to the PR description's Compatibility section, so this is
readable without the code:

> Resizing a degraded topology is refused rather than attempted. A bare fault does not
> lower `effective_ep_size`, and every cohort rendezvous sizes itself from that width, so a
> resize issued while a rank inside the width is inactive would wait on a participant that
> cannot arrive. `/scale_elastic_ep` rejects it up front, naming the inactive ranks, before
> any barrier is posted. That holds in both directions, so an `8 -> 4` whose retiring
> suffix is already short and an append grow from a degraded cohort fail the same way.
> Replacing failed capacity is the recovery path, meaning grow into the retired slots below
> the launch width, not shrink then regrow. Recovery at a nonzero launch offset, and
> retiring a set that is not the high rank suffix, both remain out of scope here.

The Mooncake recovery gap from (2) is the bullet beside it.

Net for Dynamo: every degraded topology resize fails closed at the API with the inactive ranks
named. The reconciler can choose recovery or group recreation from the rejection itself rather
than inferring it from a timeout.

On `operation_id`, I took the option you offered in your previous note and documented the
current boundary rather than widening this PR. The description now states that it is a
correlation tag and not an idempotency key: a retry carrying an id already in flight is refused
like any other concurrent resize rather than resumed, reuse with a different target is not
rejected on the id, and joining ranks are not bound to it. What a later resize does check is the
width, since the cohort record carries `target_ep_size` and a survivor refuses a join that does
not match the pending target. So a stale joiner aimed at a different width is caught, and one
aimed at the same width is not told apart from a fresh one. That last point is the reason I
would rather your three semantics land together under #35376 with a topology generation behind
them than arrive here as two of three. Two thirds would read like an idempotency key without
being one.

> Runtime scale-down is a big capability, and the per-rank FSM with store barriers is thought through. The review below is against [623be71](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/623be71c0e2c14c6e053d9fd2746c594d862e784).
> 
> **Blocking**
> 
> * The description says a shrink is refused while CUDA graphs are captured, but no such check exists, and the shrink finalizer doesn't recapture. A shrink with FULL decode graphs replays at the old width (scheduler shrink branch).
> * NIXL steady-state fault detection is gated off (the `nixl.py` combine).

@ch-wan. Thank you for the reviews. All comments are addressed. The current status of this PR has been validated with tests and rebased. Please let me know if there are further issues. I will rebase on sgl/main from time to time and validate just to keep the PR in a ready to merge state.

Each comment is answered in its own thread. The following answers questions in the quoted comments that do no belong to individual threads.

## Interaction with #33728

Agreed. I took the narrower gate. The shrink now refuses unless `attn_tp_size == 1`, rather than testing the runtime `dp_size == tp_size` pair the earlier draft did. Part of that conversion has since landed: main split `dp_size` from `num_dp_ranks` under this branch while it was out. The gate crossed that rebase untouched, which is the best evidence I can offer that it was the right predicate. If #33728 lands first, this path refuses instead of quietly retiring the wrong ranks. If this lands first, I own the conversion you list: `slot_offset`/`slot_count`, `retired_ranks`/`safe_to_terminate_ranks`,
`remove_elastic_workers`, and retiring whole replicas. The boundary is documented rather than implied.


## Smaller items from the review body

### 1. `set_fan_out` FIXED
> `set_fan_out` counts replies. After the fan out drops mid call, a retiree's reply can complete a call, and a late survivor reply then leaks into the next one.

Correct, and now fixed. Your description was exact.

The mid call lowering stays, because without it an in flight call waits on a reply from a rank
that has already called `sys.exit(0)` and hangs until the caller's own timeout. What was missing
is that the finished call can still be owed a reply by a slow survivor, and that reply landed in
the next call's `_result_values`. It both corrupted those results and could complete that call
early, counting a reply to the previous request toward this one's target.

The counter I tried first was the wrong shape, which is why my earlier answer said it was not
shippable. You cannot tell an owed reply from a legitimate one by counting: a retiree that
exited will never answer, a slow survivor will, and discarding N replies blind turns the
corruption into a hang whenever the missing one was the retiree's.

So the finished call now keeps its bucket open for a bounded window before releasing the lock.
That is what makes it sound rather than best effort: the request is sent under the same lock, so
no later call has been sent yet, and anything arriving is stale by construction. The path is
also unreachable outside a resize, since the event only fires at
`len(values) >= _result_fan_out`, so a short count means nothing else, and `set_fan_out` has no
caller but the three scale completions.

`test_fan_out_straggler.py` is new and runs in CI, 7 tests. The leak test fails against the
previous code with `99 unexpectedly found in [99, 10, 11, 12]`, which is the corruption itself:
a foreign reply counted toward a target of 3. Validated on the cluster at 16/16, `BENCH_On` and
`BENCH_Off` for the timing, since the resize itself runs over one of these communicators, and
`MC03` and `MC17` for the transitions. Admission blackout and settle both moved inside noise
against the same tree without the change.

### 2. `elastic_stage_plan` cost confirmed and documented, task FIXED
> `elastic_stage_plan` turns 2→3 (launch 4) into 2→4→3, which needs a joiner for every retired slot. The `asyncio.create_task(self._drive_next_elastic_stage(...))` result is also never referenced.

Your reading was exact and the cost was real. A partial regrow now goes direct, in the third
commit. Chasing it also showed the reason I had written in the docstring was wrong, so thank you
for the push. Details in a separate comment so this list stays readable.

The unreferenced task is fixed. It is held, so it cannot be collected mid flight.

### 3. LPLB solvers FIXED
> The LPLB solvers keep views of the pre shrink p2l map and `ep_size`. They are rebuilt only if the reshuffle succeeds.

Rebuilt unconditionally, and before the graph rebuild, since a capture replays whatever they
hold.

### 4. `scale_ready_barrier_via_store` FIXED
> `scale_ready_barrier_via_store` logs and continues on a failed post, while the retire barriers fail closed.

Fails closed now, consistent with the retire barriers.

### 5. `is_scaling()` after a fault FIXED
> After a post scale rank fault, `is_scaling()` stays True forever with nothing reported, now that `recovery_unsupported` is gone.

Reported rather than silent. A resize requested in that state is refused at admission with the
inactive ranks named, from `get_inactive_ranks()`, so an operator sees which ranks to recover
instead of a barrier timeout. @julienmancuso asked about the same state from the orchestration
side; that reply has the detail.

### 6. WORLD broadcast FIXED
> `reshuffle_for_scale` and the periodic path still `dist.broadcast` over WORLD, even though the grow map moved to the store because that broadcast can wedge.

Fixed, and digging into it found a worse version of what you described. The shrink paths already
go through the cohort scoped store helpers, `_share_p2l` and `_cohort_barrier`, falling back to
the WORLD broadcast only when no store is configured. The periodic path was the gap, and the
wedge was not the broadcast on its own.

`EPLBManager.rebalance` did already stand down during a resize, but it sat behind
`is_post_scale_rebalance`, which reads `has_scaled`. That is set at commit, or at init for a
joiner. So a server's **first** resize had it False, skipped that path, and ran
`dump_record` mid resize: an all reduce of the logical counts over WORLD, then the
`src=0` utilization broadcast in `_get_global_average_utilization_rate`. A rank still arriving
or already exited posts neither. Same family as the watchdog hang above.

It now returns early on `is_scale_pending()` before that arm, so it covers the first resize too.
The broadcast itself still goes over WORLD, which is whole at a settled width, so I left it
alone. `test_fault_poll_guard.py` covers the first shrink, the first grow, a later resize, and
a settled width where the periodic path must still run, so the guard cannot quietly disable
rebalancing.

### 7. `global_info_tensor` sync FIXED
> `global_info_tensor.sum().item()` in `dp_attn.py` adds a sync; the `.cpu()` below it already blocks.

Removed. The existing `.cpu()` covers it.

### 8. Comment placement FIXED
> A few comments sit after a `return` or are dedented to module level (the `scale_down_state.py` DRAIN branch, `elastic_ep.py` around lines 813 and 1169).

All three moved to where they apply.

@ch-wan one follow up on the `elastic_stage_plan` point. I said it deserved its own PR. I
went and tried it, it came out smaller and cleaner than I expected, so it is in this one as
a third commit rather than a promise.

### What it does

A partial regrow now goes direct. `2 -> 3` with launch 4 is one joiner, not one per retired
slot.

Your reading of the cost was exact. Chasing it also showed the reason I had written down was
wrong, so thank you for the push. The docstring blamed a `ZeroDivisionError` on an empty
replica list and `_fair_choices` is never reached. The real constraint is that a recover
joiner covers `[ep_join_rank_offset, ep_join_rank_offset + tp_size)` and sizes its expert
map to that upper bound. So only a target short of that span needs an intermediate. A joiner
booted at exactly the target never did, and that is the common case.

### Why it was not already direct

Nothing on the survivor side could tell those two joiners apart. The joiner now announces
its width to the store, in its own key space rather than the scale cohort's, since survivors
read that one to decide whether an append grow has a cohort waiting and a recover joiner
parked at the current width would answer for an unrelated grow.

The timing is what shaped the design, and it is the part worth your eye. The joiner is a
separate process the operator launches alongside the scale request, and it cannot announce
anything until it is up. Measured 11s after the request arrived, dominated by interpreter
and torch import, so no placement inside the joiner wins that race. A scheduler cannot block
that long either.

So the schedulers never wait. Each answers from a single store read: reject with
`retry_when_joiner_announces` while nobody has spoken, reject with `required_ep_size` once
the joiner is known to be wider than the target. `_scale_elastic_ep_locked` resends on an
`asyncio.sleep` until the width is known, which puts the only long wait in async code. Every
reject lands before `request_scale`, so a resend costs a round trip and never a half
committed scale.

There is no safe default without an announce, which is why there is a wait rather than a
guess. Going direct kills a joiner wider than the target at the cohort barrier. Assuming the
launch width asks a narrower one to fill slots it has no ranks for. I measured both.

### Scope

Only grows landing strictly below the launch width. A recover slot is below it by definition
and a joiner spans at most up to it, so a grow that lands there serves any joiner. Shrinks,
and grows at or above the launch width, take no new path. A timeout falls back to the launch
width, so the previous behaviour is the floor.

One supporting fix. `init_trivial` laid out the base physical width and appended the
difference, which only holds while the requested width is the larger one. A joiner regrowing
below the launch width wants fewer physical experts than the base, the difference went
negative, `append_trivial_expert_slots` no-opped on it, and the map stayed base wide while
`ep_size` disagreed. Building at whichever width is narrower is identical arithmetic
whenever the requested width is at least the base, which is every path that existed before.

### Evidence

The pair that disagrees is the point. Same code, opposite paths, decided only by what each
joiner announced:

| Lane | Joiner | Result |
|---|---|---|
| MC21 | `join_tp=1` at offset 2, announces width 3 | grows directly to 3, 10 of 10 iterations, never staged |
| MC17 | `join_tp=2` at offset 2, announces width 4 | stages through 4, 10 of 10 iterations, never direct |

Full sweep on the final tree: 41 lanes, **340 iterations, all passing, no retries,** every
one reporting a GOOD log health verdict, all on a single uniform tree stamp. That covers both
a2a backends, all four join flavours, five multi-node shapes including the `8 -> 4 -> 8 -> 4
-> 8` cycle, the four CUDA graph scale up lanes and eight benchmark lanes. Plus 104 CPU only
CI tests.

The review below is against [e74643f](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/e74643f8523abca17878a55f16e4b7c87f90f4c3).

@ch-wan @julienmancuso I rebased this PR onto current main and added one commit, 3342da3828. It keeps the decode CUDA graphs across a planned scale down.

Without it, every shrink with CUDA graphs on recaptures all decode graphs, and admission stalls for about 9 seconds. The only way to avoid that stall is to run eager, which makes decode about 5x slower. vLLM already has this functionality in [vllm-project/vllm#54985](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54985), which reuses CUDA graphs across an Elastic EP reconfiguration with NIXL EP. We think SGLang should offer the same.

The new flag is `--elastic-ep-reuse-cuda-graph`. It is off by default and requires NIXL a2a. Every rank dispatches at the buffer capacity, `max_ep_size`, and the transport masks the slots that have no live peer. A shrink then replays the graphs it already has. A scale up still recaptures for now.

Preliminary results: a 4 to 3 shrink on one H100 node with DeepSeek V2 Lite, median of three runs.

| Mode | Admission blackout | Decode p50 after shrink |
|---|---|---|
| CUDA graphs, recapture | 9.13 s | 8.27 ms |
| CUDA graphs, reuse (new flag) | 0.84 s | 8.28 ms |
| Eager | 0.84 s | 45.63 ms |

The blackout drops about 11x and matches eager mode, while decode keeps full CUDA graph speed.

I think it is a good idea to include this feature in this PR, so SGLang matches vLLM here. Your opinions would be very welcome, especially on whether the flag should stay opt in. Thank you!
